## Paper 27 Candidate Gate

A candidate may consume Paper 27 and open a `papers/27-*` directory only if
two fresh, mutually independent candidate reviewers establish every item
below conjunctively:

1. an exact public-safe headline theorem with explicit family, assumptions,
   conclusion, equality cases, and failure boundary;
2. a bounded primary-source search through the decision date, with query log
   and search limitations disclosed, novelty at least `7.5 / 10`, and no
   absolute priority claim;
3. standalone mathematical value at least `7.5 / 10` after all predecessor
   absorption and direct-collision deductions are charged;
4. proof confidence at least `9.0 / 10`, supported by a complete proof spine,
   literal formula checks, field and scheme qualifications where relevant,
   and adversarial counterexamples;
5. a direct collision matrix against Papers 12--26 and the closest verified
   published or current primary sources;
6. explicit anti-claims, excluded regimes, equality walls, and
   assumption-failure examples;
7. no dependence on a new empirical run, numerical fit, CAS certificate,
   broad finite search, or unverifiable computation for the headline theorem;
8. a credible anonymous 22--30 content-page proof-first article after all
   governance, local paths, hashes, and discovery narrative are removed; and
9. exact noncollision with the five candidates intended for the present batch,
   so that later Batch 07 papers do not become appendices to Paper 27.

Candidate reviewer R1 must independently assess theorem size, current
literature, collision, and proof plausibility. Reviewer R2 must independently
rederive the theorem-critical algebra and try to break every assumption,
without reading R1's private reasoning. A PASS artifact is the reviewer's only
permitted write and may be created only when every finding count is zero. A
failure returns `FAIL / WRITE NOTHING`; the parent may append a bounded failure
disposition to this dashboard but may not alter or retroactively repair the
review. Any correction is a separately named immutable record.

If no candidate passes, discovery restarts without consuming Paper 27. A
borderline theorem, attractive conjecture, or proof that closes only after an
undisclosed computation is recorded as `STOP`, not promoted to a project.

## Active Discovery Lanes

The Paper 27 pass searches four separated lanes before cross-lane ranking:

1. full Newton-polytope or weighted-degree transport beyond the scalar total-
   degree mechanisms of Papers 20--26, including exact cancellation control;
2. compactification or higher-dynamical-degree structure for explicit
   polynomial symplectomorphisms, without assuming that first-degree matrices
   automatically compute cohomological spectra;
3. nonstationary selector mechanisms beyond the special period-two family of
   Paper 24, but only when accompanied by a classification or realization
   theorem rather than a literal longer-period example; and
4. reversible, reciprocal, or arithmetic constraints on Hamiltonian-shear
   degree spectra beyond Paper 25's support-rank realization and Paper 26's
   planar forward/inverse bridge.

Each lane must generate multiple candidates, record killed collisions and
counterexamples, and return at most two proof-credible finalists. Scouting and
public metadata lookup may be read-only and parallel. Formal projects and all
downstream lifecycles remain strictly serial.

## Proof-First Pilot Substitution

The generic research-pipeline pilot stage is replaced by exact theorem stress
tests for this repository. Before a candidate is ranked, reviewers must check
the displayed gradients and maps, selector inequalities, invariant cones or
fans, carry terms, leading-form noncancellation, coordinate visibility,
spectral or recurrence formulas, and at least one sharp boundary or
counterexample. Small exact fixtures may expose a false statement but never
serve as evidence for a true headline theorem. GPU hours are zero by design.

## Per-Paper Serial Lifecycle

After a dual-PASS formally opens one of Papers 27--31, that paper proceeds
alone through the following lifecycle:

1. exact ten-file proof/citation/novelty source-design author stop;
2. fresh independent `SOURCE_DESIGN_PASS`;
3. strict-canonical source lock and fresh independent `SOURCE_LOCK_PASS`;
4. proof-only article plan and fresh independent `PAPER_PLAN_PASS`;
5. publication-stage scope and fresh independent scope review;
6. publication lock and fresh independent `PUBLICATION_LOCK_PASS`;
7. exact anonymous source trio (`main.tex`, mathematical commands, and
   bibliography) followed by formal source review; a repaired source requires
   a fresh reviewer and a separately frozen revision;
8. a source-bound build-profile gate with distinct mechanical and semantic
   reviews only if a custom harness is genuinely necessary; otherwise the
   standard deterministic profile is used without inventing a custom layer;
9. one-shot two-root deterministic R0 build, independent build R1, and at most
   one explicitly bounded source-revision window;
10. deterministic R1 rebuild and fresh independent build R2, or a terminal
    blocker if any time-indexed evidence obligation was missed;
11. finalization scope, lock, lifecycle-DAG validation, and independent
    finalization review;
12. exclusive raw-byte local candidate copy plus release manifest;
13. two fresh terminal rebuilds and exact receipt comparison; and
14. a sole terminal-integrity review by a role distinct from the source,
    build, finalization, and release roles, followed only then by authorized
    exact cleanup.

No stage inherits downstream authority merely because its predecessor passed.
A blocker writes no PASS artifact. Once a dual-PASS consumes a paper number,
a later terminal blocker closes that numbered project as non-release; it does
not permit a replacement candidate, retry, or alternate project under the
same number. The final effect is at most
`LOCAL_ANONYMOUS_RELEASE_ONLY` unless the user grants separate explicit
authority.

## Deterministic-Build Evidence Rules

- Every authorization identifies exact allowed paths and exactly two fresh
  mode-`0700` roots whose nonexistence is checked immediately before their
  first creation. Future paths are never pre-created or inspected.
- The environment pins `PATH`, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, `FORCE_SOURCE_DATE`,
  `TZ`, `LC_ALL`, and `LANG`; the exact executable path, stat identity, and
  hash are captured before the first build command.
- Each root receives the exact frozen source bytes and exactly one frozen
  command sequence. There is no retry, extra command, package installation,
  network access, alternate builder, root reuse, or post-hoc evidence repair.
- Invocation-time source-trio hashes, raw command statuses, logs, opening and
  closing manifests, and cross-root byte comparisons are mandatory. Later
  output equality cannot backfill a missing pre-command fact.
- Compiler, `py_compile`, import-cache, and bytecode-cache creation are
  forbidden. Any administrative Python validator uses an isolated fresh
  process with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` and direct script/stdin execution;
  cache scans occur before and after each phase. A cache byte is a hard
  action-history failure and cleanup cannot cure it.
- JSON is recursively canonicalized and independently round-tripped; unsafe
  integers, duplicate keys, non-finite values, stale aliases, and unreachable
  claims are hostile-test failures.
- PDF review covers raw bytes, object and decoded streams, dates, fonts,
  security settings, pages, visual rendering, theorem text, citations, and
  the anonymous metadata/provenance firewall. A warning is not silently
  reclassified as success.
- Failure evidence is quarantined and preserved. Nothing is overwritten or
  cleaned to manufacture a clean history. Cleanup, when authorized after
  terminal PASS, uses exact no-follow targets only.

- `BATCH_07_STATUS.md` is the controlled lifecycle dashboard. Its Material

  event remains immutable.
- `BATCH_07_IDEA_REPORT.md` does not exist at this gate. It may be created only

- Every author stop freezes an exact regular-file, non-symlink universe with
  safe POSIX relative paths, SHA-256, byte count, LF count, mode, link count,
  and a self-excluding aggregate.
- All ledger additions are physical EOF appends bound to the pre-append parent

  monotone event identifier is the only active transition authority.
- Human prose never overrides machine fields. A prose typo, duplicated line,
  stale counter, or superseded hash is historical and non-authoritative only
  after an explicit append-only disposition names the exact error and the
  canonical replacement.
- Independent reviewers author none of the artifact under review. PASS is the
  reviewer's only permitted write and only after all conjunctive checks pass.

### Exact theorem submitted to the candidate gate

Let `K` be a field of characteristic zero, let `r >= 4` and
`g >= 2r + 1`, and put `h = g - 1` and `m = r - 2`. Let

```text
P(x) = product_{i=1}^r x_i^2,
V(q) = alpha P(q) + beta q_1^g + L(q),
W(p) = gamma P(p) + delta p_r^g + N(p),
```

where `alpha,beta,gamma,delta` are nonzero. Every monomial of the independent
finite perturbation polynomials `L` and `N` has exponent vector
`a in {0,1,2}^r \ {(2,...,2)}`. Define

```text
S(q,p) = (q, p + grad V(q)),
T(q,p) = (q + grad W(p), p),
F = T composed with S.
```

Let `M = 2*1*1^T - I`. Let `A` be obtained from `M` by replacing its first
row by `h e_1^T`, let `B` be obtained from `M` by replacing its last row by
`h e_r^T`, put `C = BA`, and let `R` reverse the `r` coordinates. Then the
headline theorem to be reviewed is:

1. `F` is a polynomial symplectomorphism.
2. The strict forward cone

   ```text
   K+ = {u>0: u_i/u_1 >= 1 for i>=2,
                sum_{i=2}^r u_i/u_1 < (h-1)/2}
   ```

   and its reflected inverse cone `K- = R K+` certify every selector, carry,
   leading form, and visible coordinate for all iterates from the ordinary
   seed `1`.
3. Writing, for `n >= 1`,

   ```text
   u_n = deg_q(F^n) = C^n 1,
   w_n = deg_p(F^n) = A C^(n-1) 1,
   D = AB = R C R,
   qbar_n = deg_q(F^(-n)) = B D^(n-1) 1,
   pbar_n = deg_p(F^(-n)) = D^n 1,
   ```

   gives the coordinatewise identities

   ```text
   qbar_n = R w_n,
   pbar_n = R u_n.
   ```

   Thus the entire inverse coordinate-degree vector is the block-swap and
   endpoint reflection of the forward vector, not merely asymptotically
   comparable.
4. For every integer `n`,

   ```text
   deg(F^n) = deg(F^(-n)) = d_|n|,
   d_n = e_r^T C^n 1 = e_1^T D^n 1.
   ```

   For positive `n`, `q_r` is uniquely forward-visible and `p_1` is uniquely
   inverse-visible; `n=0` is the disclosed tied seed.
5. With

   ```text
   T0 = 2h + 4m^2 + 4m + 5,
   S0 = h^2 - 8hm(m+1) + 2h + 4,
   D0 = h^2(2m+1)^2,
   ```

   both directions obey the exact annihilating recurrence

   ```text
   d_(n+3) = T0 d_(n+2) - S0 d_(n+1) + D0 d_n,
   d_0 = 1,
   d_1 = h(2m+3),
   d_2 = h((6m+5)h + 8m^3 + 24m^2 + 26m + 12).
   ```

6. The independent `L,N` perturbations do not change any degree statement.
   Indeed, for `b=(2,...,2)` and any nonzero derivative of a permitted
   monomial, `a-e_i <= b-e_i` componentwise with at least one strict entry.
   Its weighted score is therefore strictly below the mixed skeleton row for
   every positive weight. Excluding `a=b` is essential because otherwise the
   mixed skeleton coefficient could be cancelled.

### Proof-readiness record

An independent zero-write proof adversary verified

```text
RMR=M, RAR=B, RBR=A, D=AB=RCR, D^n=RC^nR,
```

transferred all strict selector and cone-wall estimates to `K-`, checked both
inverse carries using `D-I=R(C-I)R>0`, and showed that subtraction only changes
the sign of a unique highest form. At `n=1`, with `k=2m+3`, the endpoint
selector gap is `h-k=g-2r>=1`; the inverse/forward visibility gaps reduce to

```text
(h-2m-1)k-2h >= 2m+1,
2(m+1)(h-2m-3) > 0.
```

It also verified the inverse quotient `JQJ`, the same cubic, all initial
values, and the componentwise perturbation argument. Its in-scope census was
`Blocker 0 / Major 0 / Minor 0 / Ambiguity 0`. This is discovery evidence,
not either formal candidate review and not downstream authority.

The proof package must include the following hostile cases:

- if `g=2r`, the ordinary seed ties and lies on the cone-height boundary; this
  is a proof boundary, not a claim of actual failure;
- if `g<2r`, the mixed endpoint can win, for example `r=4,g=7`;
- a zero skeleton coefficient, positive characteristic, an exponent outside
  the strict componentwise box, or the excluded top vertex can remove or tie
  a selected row;
- an invariant common cone without `B=RAR` is insufficient. For
  `A=B=[[1,1],[1,2]]`, the forward second coordinate is visible on a natural
  cone while its reflected inverse cone still has the second, not the first,
  coordinate visible.

The candidate's proof-readiness estimate is `9.3 / 10`: every theorem branch
has an exact proof route and an explicit failure boundary. The formal
reviewers must independently recompute this score.

### Bounded primary-source search through 2026-08-28

No exact source was found for reflection-dual separated Hamiltonian product
shears with the displayed coordinatewise all-iterate identity. This is a
bounded noncollision statement, not an absolute priority claim. The closest
primary sources are:

- Shafikov--Wolf, *Filtrations, hyperbolicity and dimension for polynomial
  automorphisms of C^n*, arXiv:math/0207190, DOI
  `10.1307/mmj/1070919564`: regular maps satisfy a power relation between the
  one-step forward and inverse degrees, not this selector formula.
- Bianchi--Dinh, *Every complex Henon map is exponentially mixing of all
  orders and satisfies the CLT*, arXiv:2301.13535, DOI
  `10.1017/fms.2023.110`: Henon--Sibony maps retain algebraic degrees
  `d_+^n,d_-^n` and satisfy `d_+^p=d_-^(k-p)`, but are not this shear class.
- Deserti, *Degree growth of polynomial automorphisms and birational maps:
  some examples*, arXiv:1602.04642: an explicit affine-threefold automorphism
  has unequal forward and inverse iterate degrees, so equality is not generic.
- Gomez--Meiss, *Reversors and Symmetries for Polynomial Automorphisms of the
  Plane*, arXiv:nlin/0304035, DOI `10.1088/0951-7715/17/3/012`: reversor normal
  forms in dimension two do not give the present degree-block theorem.
- Low--Pereira--Peters--Wold, *Polynomial Completion of Symplectic Jets and
  Surfaces Containing Involutive Lines*, arXiv:1308.3151, DOI
  `10.1007/s00208-015-1217-9`: symplectic kick maps and shear completions, but
  no exact iterate-degree reciprocity.
- Kanel-Belov--Grigoriev--Elishev--Yu--Zhang, *Lifting of Polynomial
  Symplectomorphisms and Deformation Quantization*, arXiv:1707.06450, DOI
  `10.1080/00927872.2018.1427255`: tame symplectic generators and
  approximation, not degree iteration.
- Dang Nguyen-Bac, *Degree growth for tame automorphisms of an affine quadric
  threefold*, arXiv:1810.09094, DOI `10.2140/ant.2024.18.1`: simultaneous
  forward/inverse growth on a different affine variety, without this exact
  formula.
- Hasselblatt--Propp, *Degree-growth of monomial maps*,
  arXiv:math/0604521: warns that degree sequences need not satisfy a constant-
  coefficient recurrence without a proved selector mechanism.
- Favre--Wulcan, *Degree growth of monomial maps and McMullen's polytope
  algebra*, arXiv:1011.2854, DOI `10.1512/iumj.2012.61.4555`, and Lin,
  arXiv:1010.6285: Newton/toric degree precedents for monomial maps, not
  additive Hamiltonian shears.
- Dang--Favre, *Spectral interpretations of dynamical degrees and
  applications*, arXiv:2006.10262, DOI `10.4007/annals.2021.194.1.5`, and
  Blanc--van Santen, arXiv:1912.01324: spectral/algebraic results for broader
  polynomial automorphisms, not exact reflected coordinate sequences.
- Grammaticos--Ramani--Carstea--Willox, *A fast algorithmic way to calculate
  the degree growth of birational mappings*, arXiv:2501.05650, DOI
  `10.3390/math13050737`: periodic corrections in birational degree
  recurrences, relevant to reserve G1 rather than a direct collision.

Query families, run separately, were:

Search limitations: English-language discoverability and indexed public
primary sources; no claim of exhaustive coverage of books, theses, unindexed
proceedings, or all non-English literature; no citation-count inference; and

The candidate makes no claim of global priority, algebraic reversibility,

## Paper 27 Candidate v1 Failure Disposition

The first independent formal candidate review was completed by the assigned
R1 novelty/standalone reviewer. It returned `FAIL / WRITE NOTHING`, and no R1
review file was created. The assigned R2 proof reviewer was stopped before any
write; no R2 review file exists. Paper 27 remains number-unconsumed.

The finding is substantive rather than a theorem-incorrectness finding. For
the entire endpoint/reflection family in E0003, the linear symplectic map

```text
H(q,p) = (R p, -R q)
```

conjugates the inverse to a member of the same forward family:

```text
H F^(-1) H^(-1) = T_(V composed with (-R)) composed with S_(W composed with R).
```

The endpoint supports and the strict componentwise box are closed under this
operation. Consequently, when the perturbations are absent, the proposed
inverse cone, reflected matrix, coordinatewise degree identities, and cubic
recurrence can all be obtained by applying Paper 22's forward theorem to the
transformed map. The box lemma is valid but is only a short robustness
corollary. The v1 proposal therefore cannot honestly claim standalone value
at the required gate merely by expanding Paper 22's proof to 24--28 pages.

R1's independent scores were:

```text
novelty: 6.4 / 10
standalone_value: 5.9 / 10
proof_readiness: 9.1 / 10
new_proof_only_content_estimate: 12--16 pages
Blocker: 0
Major: 1
Minor: 1
Ambiguity: 1
```

The Major is the hidden affine-duality/Paper-22-corollary collision. The Minor
is failure to disclose the special reversible subfamilies and the distinction
between generic and symmetric coefficients. The Ambiguity is that the v1
packet did not formalize the collected-support convention and intermediate
reflected-cone margin in the candidate statement. These findings are
disclosed, not silently repaired. The exact theorem calculations remain
useful evidence for a redesigned candidate, but they confer no number,
project, or downstream authority.

The v1 candidate is permanently closed under this candidate version. A fresh
candidate may be proposed only after an append-only redesign record that
removes the affine-duality corollary as its headline and supplies a genuinely
broader theorem (or selects a different discovery lane), followed by two new
mutually independent reviews. No review artifact, idea report, project path,
source lock, manuscript, build, release, or external effect is authorized by
this disposition.

## Paper 27 Candidate v2 Redesign

The rejected v1 is not retried. A new candidate is opened at the discovery
level only; Paper 27 is still unconsumed and no project or idea report exists.
The redesign removes the affine-duality corollary as the headline. Its main
object is a general, checkable classification of phase-resolved degree
reciprocity on finite Newton cells.

### Frozen v2 identity and scope

```text
candidate_id: phase_resolved_tropical_duality_v2
working_title: Phase-Resolved Tropical Duality for Separated Hamiltonian Shears
paper_number: unconsumed until two fresh dual PASS reviews
project_path: absent until two fresh dual PASS reviews
target_content_pages: 22--30
proof_mode: exact polyhedral and polynomial proof; exact counterexamples only
empirical_or_CAS_evidence: none
maximum_effect: LOCAL_ANONYMOUS_RELEASE_ONLY
```

Let `K` be a characteristic-zero field and let

```text
S_V(q,p) = (q, p + grad V(q)),
T_W(q,p) = (q + grad W(p), p),
F = T_W composed with S_V,
```

for arbitrary finite-support potentials `V,W`. For every gradient support row
`rho = a-e_i`, its score on a positive degree weight `u` is `rho dot u`.
Partition the positive orthant into the finitely many strict Newton cells on
which every gradient coordinate has one unique support maximizer and every
fresh gradient degree strictly beats its carried coordinate. On a cell `C`,
write the resulting linear phase maps as `A_C` for `V` and `B_C` for `W`.
The cell certificate includes the strict inequalities, algebraic independence
or another explicit leading-form survival proof, and the image-cell labels
for both phase orders. Let `R` be a coordinate permutation involution.

The v2 headline theorem is the following equivalence, with the hypotheses
stated explicitly rather than hidden in a special family.

**Phase-resolved duality theorem.** On a full-dimensional strict cell `C` and
its reflected inverse cell `R C`, assume the certificate is cancellation-free
for both plus and minus shears and that all visited cell transitions are
defined. Then the following are equivalent on every open seed set contained
in `C`:

1. The phase-resolved degree vectors of every iterate satisfy

   ```text
   deg_q(F^(-n)) = R deg_p(F^n),
   deg_p(F^(-n)) = R deg_q(F^n)       for every n >= 0;
   ```

2. Every visited cell edge has the reflected selector identity

   ```text
   B_(R C) = R A_C R,
   ```

   and the reflected cell transition sends `R C` to `R(C')` whenever the
   forward transition sends `C` to `C'`.

The forward phase is `w=A_C u`, `u'=B_C w`; the inverse phase is
`qbar=B_(R C) R u`, `pbar=A_(R C') qbar`. Sufficiency follows by induction
over the reflected cell graph. Necessity is not an asymptotic argument: at
`n=1`, equality on a full-dimensional open set gives
`B_(R C) R u = R A_C u`; equality of linear forms forces the displayed
matrix identity. If only total scalar degrees are compared, this necessity
statement is false, which is an explicit anti-claim.

**Finite-cell corollary.** For a finite Newton cell complex with a cell
involution, exact phase-resolved reciprocity is decidable by (i) strict score
and carry inequalities on each visited cell, (ii) leading-form survival, and
(iii) finitely many reflected matrix identities and edge checks. If one edge
fails an identity, an open seed in that cell is a constructive `n=1`
counterexample. The theorem does not assert that every polynomial shear has a
finite invariant cell complex; finiteness is a hypothesis to be checked.

**Strict lower-ideal stability.** A support perturbation may be added on each
cell only when every new gradient row has a strict score gap below the locked
selected row throughout the whole closed cell certificate (and the skeleton
coefficients remain nonzero). Under that explicit condition the cell graph,
matrices, leading-form proof, and both forward/inverse degree sequences are
unchanged. This is a lower-ideal theorem, not an arbitrary-lower-degree or
arbitrary-support assertion.

The endpoint-spiked Paper 22 family is one application: its `A,B,C` and
strict cone satisfy the criterion, and the previously checked
`{0,1,2}^r` componentwise lower ideal supplies a concrete stability example.
It is not the v2 headline and its forward cone/cubic are absorbed rather than
claimed as new. The finite-cell theorem also covers support pairs with no
literal potential-level reflection, provided their *selected* score maps obey
the reflected identities; lower-order support asymmetry then does not alter
the degree theorem. No claim is made that such maps are or are not affinely
conjugate as polynomial maps.

### Required proof and counterexample package

The source design must prove, in this order:

1. a precise finite-support/strict-cell definition that handles collected
   equal exponents and records coefficient nonvanishing;
2. plus/minus shear inverse phase order and a characteristic-zero leading-form
   survival lemma;
3. the reflected-cell induction for arbitrary finite cell paths, including
   phase carries and the `n=0` tie;
4. the open-set linear-identity argument proving necessity;
5. the lower-ideal perturbation theorem with a uniform closed-cell margin;
6. at least two explicit non-Paper-22 cell examples and one failure example
   where a single reflected matrix identity fails and degree reciprocity breaks
   at `n=1`;
7. an honest boundary section: cell-wall ties, support cancellation, missing
   finite invariant complexes, zero coefficients, positive characteristic,
   changed seed, and scalar-only equality;
8. a transparent application table showing exactly which lines are inherited
   from Papers 20--26 and which are proved by v2.

The two non-Paper-22 examples must be selected only after their strict cell
inequalities are symbolically verified. A proposed example that is merely an
abstract matrix without a Hamiltonian support realization is not sufficient.

### Fresh literature and collision boundary for v2

The bounded primary-source search already recorded in E0003 remains attached,
with the following changed interpretation. Newton/toric and birational
recurrence papers (Hasselblatt--Propp, Favre--Wulcan, Lin, El Hilany,
Grammaticos--Ramani--Carstea--Willox) motivate finite-cell cautions but do not
state the phase-resolved necessity/sufficiency criterion. Symplectic shear
papers (Løw--Pereira--Peters--Wold; Kanel-Belov et al.; Janeczko--Jelonek)
define the ambient maps but do not classify their degree cells. Regular-map
power relations (Shafikov--Wolf; Bianchi--Dinh) and Paper 26's scaled bridge
are explicitly adjacent, not substitutes for the open-cell matrix theorem.

The direct Paper 22 collision is now absorbed as an application and a test
fixture, not the contribution. Paper 25's support-rank factorization is not
used; v2 concerns finite-cell selector identities and necessity, not
characteristic-factor sharpness or Perron minimality. Paper 26's planar
Newton-envelope theorem is a separate specialized sufficient result and its
anti-claim against termwise equality is a motivating boundary. Papers 20, 21,
23, and 24 supply examples or different stationary/periodic mechanisms only.

Provisional v2 gate estimates (to be independently audited) are:

```text
novelty: 8.0 / 10
standalone_value: 8.1 / 10
proof_readiness: 9.0 / 10, conditional on two explicit non-Paper-22 examples
collision_risk: 4.5 / 10
```

These are not PASS scores. The candidate must not be presented as a theorem
for arbitrary support or as a generic reversibility result. The strongest
anti-claim is that scalar total-degree equality alone does not identify the
reflected selector matrices.

## V2 Explicit Example and Failure Supplement

To make the v2 page and proof gate falsifiable, the following examples are
now frozen in the status packet. They are mathematical specifications, not
experiments and not project files.

### Example A: a non-endpoint two-mode strict cell

Over any characteristic-zero field, take

```text
V(q) = q_1^3 q_2^2,
W(p) = p_1^2 p_2^3,
A = [[2,2],[3,1]],
B = R A R = [[1,3],[2,2]],
C = BA = [[11,5],[10,6]].
```

There is one support per gradient coordinate, so the strict Newton cell is
the whole positive orthant. The gradient beats its carried coordinate in both
phases for every positive weight. The cone

```text
0.5 < u_2/u_1 < 2
```

is mapped strictly into itself by
`u_2/u_1 -> (10+6(u_2/u_1))/(11+5(u_2/u_1))`; the endpoint values are
`13/13.5` and `22/21`, so the closure margins are explicit. The exponent
matrices of the two leading monomials have nonzero determinant, and products
of their leading forms remain nonzero. This realizes the v2 theorem without
an endpoint spike or the Paper 22 dimension restriction.

### Example B: a three-mode endpoint cell outside Paper 22

Take `r=3`, `g=21`, `h=20`, `m=1`, with

```text
V(q) = q_1^2 q_2^2 q_3^2 + q_1^21,
W(p) = p_1^2 p_2^2 p_3^2 + p_3^21,
A = [[20,0,0],[2,1,2],[2,2,1]],
B = [[1,2,2],[2,1,2],[0,0,20]],
C = BA = [[28,6,6],[46,5,4],[40,40,20]].
```

On `x_2,x_3 >= 1`, `sigma=x_2+x_3<19/2`, the first selector gap is
`20-1-2 sigma>0`; the second selector gap is
`36 sigma-21 x_3-6 >= 15 sigma+15>0`; the middle, last, and height wall
margins are respectively positive by
`delta+x_i-1`, `2(16)+14 sigma`, and
`15(30)`. Thus this is a finite one-cell Hamiltonian realization with a
different mode number from Paper 22 and a directly checkable reflected cell.

### Failure example: reflection identity is necessary for phase reciprocity

Take the same two-mode `V(q)=q_1^3q_2^2` but choose
`W(p)=p_1^3p_2^2`, so `A=B=[[2,2],[3,1]]` and `B != R A R`. For the open
seed `u=(1,1.2)`, the forward first-phase vector is
`A u=(4.4,4.2)`, whereas the reflected inverse first-phase vector is
`B R u=(4.4,4.6)`, not `R A u=(4.2,4.4)`. The full forward vector is
`A^2u=(17.2,17.4)` and the full inverse vector is
`A^2 R u=(18.0,17.8)`, so even scalar total degrees differ at `n=1`.
This exact rational-decimal calculation is a witness against dropping the
reflected matrix identity; it uses no numerical search.

The two positive examples and the failure witness are sufficient for the v2
candidate page estimate without repeating Paper 22's long forward proof.
Their strict inequalities and collected supports must nevertheless be
rederived in the formal proof package; this supplement is not itself a proof
lock.

## V2 Seed-Set and Cell Semantics Clarification

In the v2 theorem, an “open seed set” means a full-dimensional open subset of
the real tropical weight cell. The exact polynomial degree statement is made
for the full-dimensional integer lattice points in that cell for which the
certificate applies; the ordinary all-ones seed is a separate sufficient
application. If two linear phase maps agree on that integer set, they agree
as linear forms on the ambient span, so the `n=1` necessity argument is
legitimate. No claim is made that every real tropical weight is the degree
vector of one fixed polynomial seed.

Each strict cell records the phase-state pair (fresh degree vector and carried
degree vector), not just the fresh vector in isolation. Its defining
inequalities include the selected support score, the carried-term gap, and the
image cell for the next phase. This is the object transported by `R`; a cell
identity may not be inferred from a visually similar cone alone.

## V2 Reflected-Seed, Block, and Margin Correction

The v2 theorem compares two runs with related initial degree weights. For a
forward seed `u` in a strict cell, the inverse run is initialized with the
reflected momentum seed `R u`. Thus the exact statement is

```text
deg_q(F^(-n); R u) = R deg_p(F^n; u),
deg_p(F^(-n); R u) = R deg_q(F^n; u).
```

For the ordinary seed `1`, this is also a same-seed statement because
`R 1 = 1`. For a non-reflection-invariant seed, silently using the same seed
on both sides is not claimed and is a deliberate counterexample boundary.

The reflected action is on a phase-state pair, not one vector: if a forward
state is `(u,w)` with fresh position block `u` and carried momentum block `w`,
then its inverse counterpart is

```text
R_state(u,w) = (R w, R u).
```

The cell involution must map every strict score, carry, and image-cell
inequality under this block swap. The necessity proof uses an open cell whose
integer lattice points span the ambient vector space; equality of linear maps
on those points then forces the matrix identity.

Finally, every “uniform strict margin” is stated on a normalized compact
certificate section, for example

```text
Sigma_C = {u in closure(C): ||u||_1 = 1 and all declared strict inequalities hold}.
```

The required gap is `>= Delta > 0` on `Sigma_C`; homogeneity then gives a gap
at least `Delta ||u||_1` for nonzero weights. No positive margin is asserted
at the cone origin, and a cell whose closure contains an unremoved wall is
not called a closed strict certificate.

## V2 Full Phase-State Certificate Correction

The v2 finite-cell object is now defined in the full phase-state space. A
forward state is a pair `(u,w)` of fresh position and carried momentum degree
vectors. A strict forward cell `mathfrak C` includes, for its selected rows,

```text
A_C u > w,
B_C A_C u > u,
(B_C A_C u, A_C u) in the declared next cell.
```

The phase transition is therefore
`Phi_C(u,w)=(B_C A_C u, A_C u)`. Its inverse counterpart is obtained by the
block involution

```text
R_state(u,w) = (R w, R u),
```

and must satisfy the reflected inequalities and image-cell relation. The
selector rows themselves are support-score maxima in `u` (or `w` in the
opposite phase); the displayed strict inequalities are the carry conditions
that were previously described only informally.

All margin claims refer to a normalized compact phase-state section

```text
Sigma_C = closure(mathfrak C) intersect {||(u,w)||_1=1}
```

after imposing the declared positive ratio/lower-bound constraints that keep
the fresh block away from zero. A strict lower-ideal perturbation has a gap
`ell_selected(u)-rho dot u >= Delta_C > 0` on this full section. Homogeneity
extends it to nonzero states. No unnormalised-origin margin is claimed.

The explicit examples are full certificates, not only fresh-vector sketches.

* In Example A use the invariant ratio band
  `2/3 <= u_2/u_1 <= 3/2` and the pair cone `0<w<=u`. Directly,
  `A-I` and `C-A` are entrywise positive, so `A u>w`, `C u>A u`, and the
  next pair remains in the cone. The map
  `(10+6x)/(11+5x)` sends the band strictly into its interior.
* In Example B use `u in K+` from E0008 and `0<w<=u`. The explicit row
  inequalities give `A u>u`, `C u>A u`, and the three fresh-vector walls
  return strictly to `K+`; hence the pair transition is invariant. Reflection
  gives the complete inverse pair certificate.
* The failure example uses the reflected seed `R u` on the inverse side and
  therefore tests the corrected convention, not a same-seed mismatch.

The v2 proof must state the finite-cell theorem for these pair cells and may
not infer a carry or a perturbation margin from a fresh vector alone.

## V2 Necessity and Asymmetric Lower-Ideal Example

The phase-resolved theorem has two levels. Reflected selector identities on
every certified phase-state edge are sufficient for the block-swapped
reciprocity induction with no rank assumption. The converse is asserted only
on an edge-observable cell: the attainable intermediate set
`{A_C u}` contains a full-dimensional open set (for square matrices,
`det(A_C) != 0` is sufficient). The q-half equality at `n=1` then forces
`B_(R C)=R A_C R`; the p-half equality on the open intermediate image forces
the reflected `A` identity. Rank-deficient cells retain only the sufficient
direction and are an explicit boundary, never an implicit inference.

The following asymmetric lower-ideal realization is now part of the packet:

```text
V(q) = q_1^3 q_2^2 + epsilon q_1^2,
W(p) = p_1^2 p_2^3 + eta p_1^2,
epsilon, eta != 0.
```

The dominant rows remain `A=[[2,2],[3,1]]` and
`B=[[1,3],[2,2]]=R A R`; the extra rows are `(1,0)` and `(1,0)`, strictly
below their respective mixed rows on the ratio band `2/3 <= u_2/u_1 <= 3/2`.
The perturbations are deliberately not related by coordinate reflection (the
reflection of the first extra support would be `(0,1)`). Hence the standard
swap/reflection `H(q,p)=(R p,-R q)` does not map this chosen pair to itself,
while the selected-cell theorem still gives exact reflected degree vectors.
This statement excludes only that particular self-conjugacy; it makes no
claim about other polynomial conjugacies or reversors. Examples A and B have
`det A=-4` and `-60`; Example C here has the same full-rank dominant `A` and
supplies the non-literal-reflection application needed for standalone value.

## Paper 27 Candidate v2 Failure Disposition

The fresh v2 R1 review again returned `FAIL / WRITE NOTHING`; no v2 review
file was created. R2 was instructed to stop before writing and has created no
artifact. Paper 27 remains number-unconsumed.

The mathematics is not rejected wholesale, but the frozen v2 wording still
had four active gate findings:

1. The headline equivalence and finite-cell corollary still said that any
   failed edge identity yields an open `n=1` counterexample, while E0012
   limited the converse to edge-observable cells. On a rank-deficient edge,
   the reflected maps may agree on the reachable image and differ on a
   complementary subspace; the asserted counterexample need not exist.
2. The second-phase identity was described in prose but not given an explicit
   phase-labelled condition. A valid pair requires both
   `B_(R C)=R A_C R` and `A_(R C')=R B_(C') R` on each directed edge, with
   the source/target phase labels fixed.
3. The packet alternated between a full `2r`-dimensional phase-state cell and
   a diagonal initial pair `(u,u)` without stating which quantifier powered
   the converse. The corrected theorem must use full pair states for
   sufficiency and either an edge-observable open intermediate image or an
   explicitly stated diagonal-seed limitation for necessity.
4. Example A said `A-I` was entrywise positive, but
   `A-I=[[1,2],[3,0]]`; the needed vector inequality is positive on the
   declared ratio band, not entrywise positivity.

The independent v2 score was `novelty 7.7`, `standalone 7.3`, and `proof
readiness 8.2`, with `Blocker 0 / Major 1 / Minor 2 / Ambiguity 2`. The
failure is therefore a gate failure, not evidence that the proposed corrected
theorem is false. All v2 claims remain historical discovery material only.

## Paper 27 Candidate v3 — phase-cell graph theorem (frozen for fresh review)

The v2 candidate is retired.  This v3 packet is a new candidate and does not
consume a paper number or create a paper directory.  Its purpose is to state a
strictly weaker but actually closed theorem, while making the phase-state
quantifiers and the two inverse phases explicit.

### Candidate identity and scope

```text
candidate_id: phase_resolved_tropical_duality_v3
title: Phase-Resolved Tropical Duality for Finite Selector Cell Graphs
paper_number_consumed: false
scope: separated Hamiltonian polynomial shears, characteristic zero, finite
  strict Newton-selector/carry certificate, positive integral weight seeds
  in full-dimensional phase-state cells
novelty_target: a certificate-conditioned finite directed cell-graph theorem
  with coordinatewise reflected phase-state reciprocity and an observable-span
  converse; not a generic reversibility theorem
proof_target_pages: 24-28 (including examples, collision absorption, and
  limitations)
external_effect: none; no submission, upload, DOI, or communication
next_gate: BATCH07_PAPER27_CANDIDATE_V3_DUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED
```

The theorem is deliberately about weighted leading-degree transport, not about
map-level conjugacy, entropy, or a claim for every support.  A finite strict
certificate is part of the hypothesis: it records the selected support row,
all selector gaps, all carry gaps, wall preservation, and leading-form
survival for every directed edge.  Consequently the result says “finitely
checkable relative to the supplied certificate”; it does not claim an
unconditional decision algorithm over an arbitrary characteristic-zero field.

### Phase-state semantics (canonical notation)

Let (R) reverse the (r) coordinates and define the state involution
\[
  \mathscr R(u,w):=(Rw,Ru).
\]
Here (u) is the current (q)-block weight and (w) is the current
(p)-block weight.  A cell is a full-dimensional open polyhedral set
\(​\mathcal C_{\sigma,\tau,\sigma'}\subset\mathbb R_{>0}^{2r}\) of pairs
\((u,w)), together with its positive integer points.  The first (V) shear
selects a matrix (A_\sigma) and the second (W) shear selects (B_\tau):
\[
 v=A_\sigma u,
 \qquad A_\sigma u>w,
 \qquad u'=B_\tau v,
 \qquad B_\tau v>u,
\]
and the strict certificate places
\((u',v)=\Phi_e(u,w)) in the target cell
\(\mathcal C_{\sigma',\tau',\sigma''}).  Thus a directed edge is
\(e=(\sigma,\tau,\sigma')), with
\[
  \Phi_e(u,w)=(B_\tau A_\sigma u,A_\sigma u).
\]
All displayed inequalities are componentwise and are required with a positive
margin on the normalized compact section used by the certificate.

The reflected directed edge is denoted
\(\bar e=(\bar\tau,\bar\sigma',\bar\sigma)): its first inverse phase is
the W selector (B_{\bar\tau}) acting on (Ru), and its second inverse phase
is the V selector (A_{\bar\sigma'}) acting on (Rv).  The two required
phase-labelled identities are, explicitly,
\[
  B_{\bar\tau}=R A_\sigma R,
  \qquad
  A_{\bar\sigma'}=R B_\tau R.                 \tag{P27.1}
\]
They imply the state transition identity
\[
  \Phi_{\bar e}(\mathscr R(u,w))
    =\mathscr R(\Phi_e(u,w)),                 \tag{P27.2}
\]
because (B_{\bar\tau}Ru=R A_\sigma u=Rv) and
\(A_{\bar\sigma'}Rv=R B_\tau v=Ru'\).

The exact weighted-degree assertion is always quantified on the pair
\((u,w)), not on an undefined one-vector shorthand.  In particular, the
inverse run starts at (mathscr R(u,w)=(Rw,Ru)).  A same-seed statement is a
separate corollary and is allowed only when the initial pair is
\(mathscr R\)-invariant (for example (u=w=\mathbf1)).

### Proposed theorem and the correctly limited converse

**Theorem (finite reflected selector graph).**  For every edge (e) in a
finite strict certificate, if (P27.1) holds for its reflected edge, then for
every positive integral seed pair in the edge cell, induction along the
reflected path gives exact phase-state reciprocity at every iterate:
\[
  (\deg_q(F^{-n};\mathscr R(u,w)),
   \deg_p(F^{-n};\mathscr R(u,w)))
  =\mathscr R\bigl(\deg_q(F^{n};u,w),
                     \deg_p(F^{n};u,w)\bigr),
\]
with the two components interpreted as the carried (q,p) weight vectors.
The scalar total-degree equality is only a projection of this statement.

**Observable-span converse.**  Suppose the two phase-resolved equalities hold
on all positive integral pairs in one open edge cell.  Put
\[
 U_e=\operatorname{span}\{u:(u,w)\in\mathcal C_e^{\mathbb Z}\},
 \qquad
 V_e=\operatorname{span}\{A_\sigma u:(u,w)\in\mathcal C_e^{\mathbb Z}\}.
\]
Then the q-half equality forces
\[
 (B_{\bar\tau}R-R A_\sigma)u=0\quad(u\in U_e),
\]
and the p-half equality forces
\[
 (A_{\bar\sigma'}R-R B_\tau)v=0\quad(v\in V_e).
\]
Only when (U_e=\mathbb R^r) (respectively (V_e=\mathbb R^r)) may these be
upgraded to the corresponding full matrix identity in (P27.1).  If a
selector is rank deficient, equality on its reachable image does not identify
its action on a complementary subspace; no open (n=1) counterexample is
claimed from an identity failure outside that observable span.  This rank split
replaces the false unconditional “equivalence” and “every failure gives a
counterexample” wording in v2.

The proof package will separate (i) strict leading-form/carry induction, (ii)
the algebraic reflection calculation, and (iii) the linear-span argument.
No cancellation argument is used without the edge certificate, and no claim
is made across a tie wall, zero coefficient, or support cancellation.

### Frozen worked examples and stress tests

1. **Non-endpoint two-mode edge (corrected positivity statement).**  For
   (V=q_1^3q_2^2, W=p_1^2p_2^3),
   \[
   A=\begin{pmatrix}2&2\\3&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
   B=\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\2&2\end{pmatrix},\quad
   C=BA=\begin{pmatrix}11&5\\10&6\end{pmatrix}.
   \]
   On (2/3\le u_2/u_1\le3/2),
   ((A-I)u=(u_1+2u_2,3u_1)>0) and
   ((C-A)u=(9u_1+3u_2,7u_1+5u_2)>0); the proof does not say that (A-I)
   is entrywise positive.  The reflected edge uses (RAR=B).

2. **Endpoint cubic fixture (absorbed, not itself the novelty).**  With
   (r=3,g=21,h=20),
   \[
   A=\begin{pmatrix}20&0&0\\2&1&2\\2&2&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
   B=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&2\\2&1&2\\0&0&20\end{pmatrix},\quad
   C=BA=\begin{pmatrix}28&6&6\\46&5&4\\40&40&20\end{pmatrix}.
   \]
   The strict cone and carry inequalities are checked on the declared
   compact subcone; the example is used to verify phase labels and reflection,
   not to claim a new cubic (Paper22 already owns that fixture).

3. **Asymmetric lower-ideal perturbation.**  Starting with
   (V=q_1^3q_2^2, W=p_1^2p_2^3), add independently
   \(\epsilon q_1^2\) and \(\eta p_1^2\).  Their derivative rows are strictly
   below the selected rows on the positive cone, but the standard
   (H(q,p)=(Rp,-Rq)) does not map this support pair to itself (the reflected
   (q_1^2) term would lie on (p_2^2)).  This only excludes that specified
   self-conjugacy; it makes no claim that another reversor cannot exist.

4. **Genuine two-cell Hamiltonian path.**  For
   (V=W=q_1^4q_2^2+q_1^2q_2^4), on (u_1>u_2>0) the first selector is
   \[
   A_L=\begin{pmatrix}3&2\\4&1\end{pmatrix},
   \]
   and (A_Lu) lies in the opposite ordering cell.  The next selector is
   \[
   B_R=\begin{pmatrix}1&4\\2&3\end{pmatrix},\qquad
   C=B_RA_L=\begin{pmatrix}19&6\\18&7\end{pmatrix},
   \]
   with (u'_1-u'_2=u_1-u_2).  On a compact subcone away from the wall,
   (A_Lu>u) and (Cu>A_Lu) have positive margins.  The reflected path is a
   distinct inverse cell path, so this is not another one-cell endpoint
   instance; all phase labels and margins will be written out in the proof.

5. **Scalar-equality anti-witness.**  Let (R=I),
   (V=q_1^3+q_2^4), (W=p_1^4+p_2^3).  Then
   (A=\operatorname{diag}(2,3)), (B=\operatorname{diag}(3,2)), and
   (BA=AB=6I).  All scalar total degrees are (6^n), while the phase
   vectors are (Au=(2u_1,3u_2)) and (Bu=(3u_1,2u_2)).  Thus scalar equality
   cannot identify selector matrices; Paper27's claim is genuinely
   phase-resolved.

For a lower-ideal row perturbation, the certificate records a normalized
compact section \(\Sigma_e\) and checks
\[
 \max_{x\in\Sigma_e}(\ell_i-\rho)\!\cdot x\ge\Delta_e>0
\]
for every selected row \(\ell_i\).  With a supplied polyhedral certificate
this reduces to finitely many vertex inequalities.  The statement is not an
arbitrary-support or arbitrary-field decidability claim.

### Collision absorption and anti-claims

The introduction and related-work ledger will explicitly absorb P20's
visibility/spectral framework, P22's endpoint cone/cubic and box stability,
P24's selector exchange and periodic cell transitions, P25's support-rank and
minimal-recurrence results, and P26's separate forward/inverse Newton-envelope
recurrences.  Paper27 claims only the finite phase-state reflected criterion
and its observable-span converse; it does not repackage P22's cubic, P24's
period-two graph, P25's Perron/rank theorem, or P26's rate-only bridge as new
results.  The public collision screen remains “no exact direct collision
found” rather than a priority assertion.

The following are permanent anti-claims: no same-seed reciprocity for a
non-\(\mathscr R\)-invariant pair; no full-matrix necessity on a non-full
reachable span; no inference from scalar equality; no crossing of cell walls or
ties; no arbitrary-support theorem; no map-level reversibility, entropy or
higher dynamical-degree conclusion; no global classification or priority
claim; and no external effect.

### Scalar anti-witness canonicalization (standard coordinate reversal)

The scalar anti-witness in the v3 packet is strengthened to stay inside the
standard coordinate-reversal convention.  Take (R) to be the (2\times2)
coordinate swap, (V=q_1^3+q_2^4), and (W=p_1^7+p_2^5).  Then
\[
 A=\operatorname{diag}(2,3),\qquad B=\operatorname{diag}(6,4),
 \qquad BA=AB=12I,
\]
while (B\ne RAR=\operatorname{diag}(3,2)).  On any strict selector cone
with the old block below the selected diagonal rows, the forward and inverse
scalar total degrees are both (12^n), but the phase vectors are transported
by (A) and (B), respectively.  Thus scalar equality alone cannot identify
the reflected selector identities even in the standard (R)-reversal class.
The earlier (R=I) display is retained only as an algebraic shorthand and is
not used as the in-class witness.

## Canonical v3 notation replacement

The v3 prose block above was emitted with a display-escape defect in a few
inline formulas (some delimiters became literal parentheses).  The following
plain-text specification is the authoritative mathematical reading for the
fresh review.  It supersedes only display notation, not the candidate scope
or any machine event.

For a pair-state cell C[e] of positive weights (u,w), let A[sigma] be the
selected V-gradient row matrix, set v = A[sigma] u, and require the strict
carry inequality v > w.  Let B[tau] be the selected W-gradient row matrix,
set u-prime = B[tau] v, and require u-prime > u.  The edge map is

    Phi_e(u,w) = (u-prime,v) = (B[tau] A[sigma] u, A[sigma] u).

The coordinate reversal is the linear involution R; the pair-state involution
is Rstate(u,w) = (R w,R u).  The reflected edge starts its inverse W phase on
R u and its inverse V phase on R v.  Its two and only two selector conditions
are

    B[bar_tau] = R A[sigma] R,
    A[bar_sigma-prime] = R B[tau] R.

Consequently Phi_bar_e(Rstate(u,w)) = Rstate(Phi_e(u,w)).  The forward and
inverse exact weighted-degree vectors are compared on pair seeds (u,w) and
Rstate(u,w), respectively.  A same-seed assertion is allowed only for an
Rstate-fixed pair.

For the positive integer seeds in one cell define

    U_e = span of {u : (u,w) is an integer seed in C[e]},
    V_e = span of {A[sigma]u : (u,w) is an integer seed in C[e]}.

The q-half equality gives (B[bar_tau] R - R A[sigma])u = 0 on U_e, and the
p-half equality gives (A[bar_sigma-prime] R - R B[tau])v = 0 on V_e.  Full
matrix identities are concluded only when the corresponding span is all of
R^r.  No claim is made about an identity failure on an unobservable
complement.  All cells, margins, and leading-form survival statements are
relative to the finite strict certificate; finitely checkable always means
given that certificate.

The exact in-class scalar anti-witness uses the standard coordinate swap R,
V=q1^3+q2^4, and W=p1^7+p2^5.  Here A=diag(2,3), B=diag(6,4), and
BA=AB=12 I while B is not R A R.  Scalar totals agree as 12^n although the
phase vectors differ.  The earlier R=I display is non-authoritative shorthand
only.

E0018 is retained as a historical, non-authoritative append because its parent
hash/byte fields were copied before the immediately preceding append and its
manifest digest contains a transcription error.  It therefore opens no gate.
This explicit disposition is the only authority for that defect.

The v3 lower-ideal certificate also uses the following corrected condition.
For every selected row ell and lower row rho, require

    for all x in Sigma_e: (ell-rho) dot x >= Delta_e > 0,

equivalently `min` over the compact section is at least Delta_e.  A linear
score's minimum, not its maximum, is what reduces the uniform check to the
finite vertices of a supplied polyhedral certificate.

The canonical phase-state specification remains: Phi_e(u,w) =
(B[tau]A[sigma]u,A[sigma]u), Rstate(u,w)=(Rw,Ru), and the reflected edge
conditions are B[bar_tau]=R A[sigma] R and A[bar_sigma-prime]=R B[tau] R.
The converse is restricted to the spans U_e and V_e defined in E0018; full
matrix necessity requires those spans to be all of R^r.

## Reachable-edge hypothesis made explicit

The fresh mechanics audit identified a quantifier shortcut in the v3 theorem
prose.  The phrase “for every edge” is now to be read as a global hypothesis
on the finite subgraph reachable from the chosen seed, not as a one-edge
identity that magically proves all iterates.  More precisely, let
G_reach(e0) contain every forward edge visited by a seed and every reflected
edge visited by its Rstate image.  For every edge in this closed subgraph the
certificate must provide (a) the strict selector and carry gaps, (b) the
target-cell inclusion, (c) the reflected edge and its own strict certificate,
and (d) both phase identities

    B[bar_tau] = R A[sigma] R,
    A[bar_sigma-prime] = R B[tau] R.

Only under this closed reachable-subgraph hypothesis does induction yield the
n-step phase-state identity.  A single certified edge yields only the
corresponding one-step statement.  The identities alone do not assert the
reflected cell inequalities or target labels; those are separate certificate
items.  The observable-span converse remains one-edge and is unchanged.

## Paper 27 Candidate v3 Failure Disposition

Both fresh v3 reviewers returned `FAIL / WRITE NOTHING`; neither v3 review
artifact was created.  E0020 repaired the all-iterate quantifier, but it did
not cure the candidate's standalone and application defects.  Paper 27 is
still number-unconsumed.

The decisive R1 and R2 findings were:

1. The proposed graph theorem assumed an exact strict leading-form
   certificate and then performed an elementary intertwining induction.  It
   did not derive the hard selector, carry, noncancellation, and reflected
   cell facts from a sufficiently broad support class.  After P24/P26
   absorption, that conditional result was too close to a technique lemma.
2. Example D showed an L-to-R-to-L pair of selector phases, but its full-step
   label was a self-loop under the packet's own cell convention.  It supplied
   no open full pair-state w-domain, target cell, reflected target, integer
   seed set, or normalized margins.  Its symmetric dominant support also has
   the standard H reversor; Example C broke only that H with degree-invisible
   lower rows and did not create a new graph.
3. The lower-ideal margin still lacked separate V- and W-phase projections;
   the row score lives in r dimensions while the normalized pair section
   lives in 2r dimensions.
4. The scalar anti-witness needed an ordinary-seed or norm normalization and
   the inverse phase vector B R u.  The examples also mixed an open pair cell
   with a closed inequality convention.

R1's final estimates after E0020 were approximately novelty 6.8, standalone
6.2, proof readiness 7.8, and 16--21 credible pages.  R2 independently found
Blocker 0 / Major 1 / Minor 2 / Ambiguity 2 and scored novelty 7.3,
standalone 7.0, proof readiness 8.5, and 18--21 pages.  The candidate therefore
fails multiple conjunctive thresholds even though its local matrix algebra is
valid.  A v4 candidate must be support-derived rather than certificate-
tautological and must include a genuine nontrivial full pair-state realization.

## Paper 27 Candidate v4 — support-derived Newton-fan automata

The v3 candidate is closed.  This v4 packet is a new, number-free candidate
whose central result is support-derived rather than a conditional matrix
induction.  It combines a finite normal-fan construction, a coefficient-
uniform Hessian/Jacobian noncancellation lemma, and a reflected reachable-
subgraph classification.

### Candidate identity and gate target

~~~text
candidate_id: newton_fan_hessian_automata_v4
title: Newton-Fan Automata and Phase Reciprocity for Hamiltonian Shears
paper_number_consumed: false
family: finite collected polynomial supports in characteristic zero; separated
  Hamiltonian position and momentum shears; strict positive weighted degrees
headline: support-derived exact phase automata are reciprocal on and only on
  the observable spans of a reflection-closed reachable subgraph, provided
  every exposed face has a private Hessian transversal
new_content: normal-fan construction + coefficient-uniform leading survival +
  observable-span iff criterion + asymmetric three-dimensional two-node
  realization
proof_target_pages: 24-29 content pages
external_effect: none
next_gate: BATCH07_PAPER27_CANDIDATE_V4_DUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED
~~~

### Support-level construction (no survival assumption)

Let K be a characteristic-zero field.  Write

    V(q) = sum_{alpha in E_V} c_alpha q^alpha,
    W(p) = sum_{beta  in E_W} d_beta p^beta,

where E_V and E_W are finite collected subsets of nonnegative integer
vectors, all displayed coefficients are nonzero, and q,p have the same r
coordinates.  For each derivative row i use the active sets
E_V,i = {alpha in E_V : alpha_i > 0} and E_W,i analogously.  A row score is
alpha dot u minus u_i.  The common refinement of the finitely many strict
score inequalities, together with positive carry inequalities, is a finite
rational polyhedral phase graph.  On a strict cell each row has a unique
exposed exponent; its selector matrices are

    A_sigma[i,*] = alpha_sigma,i - e_i,
    B_tau[i,*]   = beta_tau,i  - e_i.

The pair-state node is an open set of (u,w) in R_{>0}^{2r}; its edge map is

    v = A_sigma u,
    v > w,
    u-prime = B_tau v,
    u-prime > u,
    Phi_e(u,w) = (u-prime,v).

Target-cell inclusion is an exact implication between rational linear
inequalities.  A finite Farkas multiplier certificate is sufficient and is
part of the public proof data; it is not a numerical search or a CAS oracle.
The graph is generated from the supports and these implications, rather than
postulated independently.

### Private Hessian transversal and exact leading survival

For a selected exposed face F of a support polynomial, let P_F be its face
polynomial.  A private Hessian transversal consists of a permutation pi and
one face monomial alpha^(i) for each Hessian entry (i,pi(i)) such that the
determinant expansion term has a nonzero derivative coefficient and its
combined variable exponent

    sum_i (alpha^(i) - e_i - e_{pi(i)})

occurs in no other determinant term of Hess(P_F).  The condition is checked
in the collected support, including all r-fold choices and permutations.  In
the important single-monomial case alpha^(i)=alpha for every i and all
alpha_i are positive, the private coefficient is explicit:

    det Hess(c_alpha X^alpha)
      = c_alpha^r (-1)^r (1 - |alpha|) product_i alpha_i
        X^(r alpha - 2 one).

It is nonzero in characteristic zero.  Hence every private transversal makes
det Hess(P_F) a nonzero polynomial for every choice of nonzero face
coefficients.  The Jacobian criterion gives algebraic independence of the
components of grad P_F.  Substitution into an algebraically independent
leading tuple is injective, so the selected leading forms cannot cancel.
Strict carry gaps then make the fresh gradient block dominate the old block.
Induction applies separately to forward shears and to the subtraction phases
of the inverse; signs change coefficients but not exponent rows.  Thus exact
weighted-degree transport is derived from supports, rather than assumed as a
certificate input.

### Main theorem (support-derived phase automaton)

For any finite support pair whose reachable strict normal-fan cells have
private Hessian transversals and exact Farkas-certified selector/carry/target
inclusions, the following hold.

1. Literal differentiation, the symmetric-Hessian calculation, and the
   triangular inverse formulas make F = S_W composed with T_V a polynomial
   symplectomorphism.  On every reachable cell the actual forward and inverse
   leading-degree vectors equal the support-derived piecewise-linear orbit;
   this includes arbitrary nonzero coefficient choices and inverse minus
   signs.
2. Let R reverse coordinates and let Rstate(u,w) = (R w,R u).  Require a
   finite reachable subgraph closed under Phi and under Rstate, with a strict
   reflected certificate on every reflected edge.  If e=(sigma,tau,sigma-prime)
   and its reflected inverse edge is bar-e=(bar-tau,bar-sigma-prime,bar-sigma),
   then phase reciprocity holds exactly when the following two identities hold
   on the relevant observable spans:

       B[bar-tau] R u = R A[sigma] u,
       A[bar-sigma-prime] R v = R B[tau] v,
       v = A[sigma]u.

   If the seed spans are full, these become the two matrix identities
   B[bar-tau] = R A[sigma] R and
   A[bar-sigma-prime] = R B[tau] R.  Otherwise the theorem makes no claim on
   the complementary unobservable subspace.
3. Conversely, equality of both phase-resolved vectors on all positive
   integer seeds of an edge forces exactly those two restrictions.  Scalar
   total-degree equality alone is explicitly insufficient.
4. The criterion is finite: enumerate exposed faces, compute the common fan,
   solve the strict rational cone implications, test private transversals,
   and inspect the finite reflected reachable graph.  “Finite” means finite
   relative to the displayed support and exact certificate; no unconditional
   algorithm over arbitrary fields is claimed.

The inverse phase ordering is fixed, not implicit.  On a reflected pair
(x,y)=(R w,R u), the first inverse output is B[bar-tau] y and the second is
A[bar-sigma-prime] B[bar-tau] y.  It equals (R v,R u-prime), the reflected
next pair.  Same-seed reciprocity is stated only for Rstate-fixed pairs.

### Phase-projected lower-ideal stability

If a new support row rho is added below a selected V row ell on the projected
u-section Sigma_e^V, require for every x in Sigma_e^V

    (ell-rho) dot x >= Delta_V > 0.

For a W row use the projected fresh-v section Sigma_e^W and require the
analogous inequality with Delta_W.  These are minima/forall conditions, not
maxima on a 2r-dimensional pair section.  For rational compact polytopes a
linear score is checked at finitely many vertices.  The row remains inactive,
the same automaton and private-transversal proof applies, and the added term
may be chosen independently on the two potentials.  This is a bounded
lower-ideal corollary, not arbitrary-support robustness.

### Exact asymmetric two-node realization (r = 3)

Use coordinate reversal R(1,2,3)=(3,2,1) and supports

    E_V = { a1=(8,2,2), a2=(2,5,6), gamma=(2,8,2) },
    E_W = { b1=R a1=(2,2,8), b2=R a2=(6,5,2) }.

All coefficients are arbitrary nonzero elements of K.  The gamma vertex is
genuinely active elsewhere (at u=(1,2,1), gamma has the largest score), but
its reflected partner R gamma is absent from E_W.  Therefore the full
support pair is not globally R-related and the standard map-level reversor
H(q,p)=(R p,-R q) is not an explanation for the local degree reciprocity.
No assertion is made that another reversor cannot exist.

For a monomial alpha put A_alpha = one alpha^T - I.  The relevant matrices are

    A1 = [[7,2,2],[8,1,2],[8,2,1]],
    A2 = [[1,5,6],[2,4,6],[2,5,5]],
    Ag = [[1,8,2],[2,7,2],[2,8,1]],
    B1 = [[1,2,8],[2,1,8],[2,2,7]],
    B2 = [[5,5,2],[6,4,2],[6,5,1]].

Define two full-dimensional open positive cones

    N1:  6u1 - 3u2 - 4u3 > 0,   u1 - u2 > 0,
    N2: -6u1 + 3u2 + 4u3 > 0,   4u3 - 3u2 > 0,

and pair cells

    C1-plus = {(u,w): u in N1, 0 < w < A1 u},
    C2-plus = {(u,w): u in N2, 0 < w < A2 u}.

The inequalities are componentwise.  The first phase in C1-plus selects a1;
after it, W selects b2 because

    (b2-b1) dot A1 u = 4u1 - u2 + 8u3 > 0.

The full product is

    C1 = B2 A1 = I + one (90,19,22)^T.

It sends C1-plus into C2-plus because the target N2 gaps are

    (a2-a1) dot C1 u = (84,22,26) dot u,
    (a2-gamma) dot C1 u = (90,16,26) dot u,

and the target first-carry gap is

    A2 C1 u - A1 u = one (1074,231,268)^T dot u,

all strictly positive.  The reflected inverse edge uses b1 first and a2
second; its gamma gap is

    (a2-gamma) dot R A1 u = (4,5,2) dot u > 0.

In C2-plus the first phase selects a2 and W selects b2, since

    (b2-b1) dot A2 u = (-2,2,12) dot u > 0.

The product is

    C2 = B2 A2 = I + one (18,55,70)^T.

It preserves C2-plus: the four defining gaps after one step have coefficient
vectors

    (a2-a1) dot C2 u       = (12,58,74) dot u,
    (a2-gamma) dot C2 u     = (18,52,74) dot u,
    (b2-b1) dot A2 C2 u     = (216,660,840) dot u,
    (a2-gamma) dot R A2 C2 u= (216,? ,?) dot u,

with the last line obtained directly from the displayed matrices and retained
as an exact positive linear form in the proof.  More directly, before the
step the reflected gamma gap is h2=(-2,8,6) dot u and after the step it is
h2+12(18u1+55u2+70u3), hence strictly larger.  The target pair carry is

    A2 C2 u - A2 u = one (216,660,840)^T dot u > 0.

Thus the support-derived graph has two distinct full pair-state nodes
C1-plus -> C2-plus -> C2-plus.  Its reflected graph is
C1-minus -> C2-minus -> C2-minus, where Cj-minus=Rstate(Cj-plus), with the
two phase identities checked literally.  A rational compact inner section is
obtained by normalizing u1+u2+u3=1, imposing each listed strict gap at least
1/1000, and replacing the open w bound by w_i <= 999/1000 (A_j u)_i;
the coefficient vectors above give the target margins.  Integer seeds are
obtained by clearing denominators.  For example (u,w)=((2,1,1),(1,1,1)) is
in C1-plus, while the ordinary pair ((1,1,1),(1,1,1)) is in C2-plus; the
ordinary seed is not claimed to traverse the transient C1 node.

Each selected monomial has all coordinates at least two, so its private
Hessian determinant is nonzero by the explicit formula.  The gamma chamber is
excluded only because the theorem is restricted to the reflection-closed
reachable component C1-plus union C2-plus; no global support symmetry is
silently assumed.

### Sharp failure fixtures and collision accounting

Removing the private-transversal condition is substantive.  Take
V=(q1+q2+q3)^3.  Its Hessian is rank one and the three leading gradient forms
coincide.  With W=(p1-p2)^3, the first W-gradient vanishes on that leading
tuple, giving an explicit n=2 leading cancellation.  This is outside the
admissible class and is the boundary example for the Hessian hypothesis.

Removing a reachable reflected identity gives an open integer-seed n=1
phase-vector mismatch by the observable-span converse.  Removing a reflected
cell certificate, or allowing a tie wall, voids the exact-degree conclusion.

The collision matrix charges P20 for visibility and stationary matrices, P22
for endpoint cones and cubic quotients, P24 for its special planar period-two
monodromy, P25 for support-rank/Perron factorization, and P26 for planar
Newton-envelope recurrences and the rate-only forward/inverse bridge.  The
new contribution is the support-derived private-Hessian automaton and its
observable reflection classification in r>=3 mixed-support cells; no old
recurrence, period-two example, or map-level reversor is relabelled as new.
The public 2026-08-28 primary-source screen (Gomez--Meiss; Shafikov--Wolf;
Hasselblatt--Propp; Bedford--Kim; Favre--Wulcan; Fordy--Hone;
Blanc--van Santen; El Hilany; Takenawa; and the recent tropical/Newton
polyhedral papers) found no exact conjunction.  This is not a priority claim.

Permanent anti-claims: no arbitrary support or arbitrary field decidability;
no claims on non-private faces, ties, zero coefficients, positive
characteristic, unobservable complements, gamma's separate chamber, global
map reversibility, entropy, higher dynamical degrees, global classification,
or same-seed reciprocity for a non-Rstate-fixed pair.  No build, upload,
submission, or other external effect is authorized.

## Paper 27 v4 arithmetic and certificate corrections

The v4 packet is retained, but three exact readings are made canonical for
review.  First, in the C2 reflected-gamma line the placeholder vector is
replaced by

    (a2-gamma) dot R A2 C2 u = (214,668,846) dot u.

Second, the strict normal cones include every gap used by either forward or
reflected phase, not just a generating subset:

    N1: g12>0, g1gamma>0, d1=(b2-b1) dot A1 u>0,
        h1=(a2-gamma) dot R A1 u>0;
    N2: g21>0, g2gamma>0, d2=(b2-b1) dot A2 u>0,
        h2=(a2-gamma) dot R A2 u>0.

The first two inequalities displayed in E0022 imply the latter two, but they
are now listed explicitly so the reflected selector certificate is visible.
The pair cells remain the open sets 0<w<A_i u; their normalized inner
sections use strict componentwise margins and a rational denominator.

Third, a private Hessian transversal always includes a nonzero determinant
coefficient condition: the selected derivative factors, collected nonzero
face coefficients, and the corresponding Hessian minor must be nonzero in K.
For a single monomial this is guaranteed by alpha_i>0 and |alpha|>1 in
characteristic zero; for a multi-monomial face uniqueness is required among
all permutations and all r-fold face-support choices.  Exponent uniqueness by
itself is never treated as sufficient.

In the target-carry notation, the vector statement
`A2 C1 u - A1 u = one (1074,231,268) dot u` means the three-vector all of
whose entries equal 1074u1+231u2+268u3; the analogous C2 statement has
entries 216u1+660u2+840u3.

## Paper 27 v4 canonical theorem and fixture replacement

The following replaces the ambiguous portions of E0022 while preserving its
candidate identity.  The map convention is fixed as

    S_V(q,p) = (q, p + grad V(q)),
    T_W(q,p) = (q + grad W(p), p),
    F = T_W composed with S_V.

The support graph is generated from the common refinement of the row-wise
Newton normal fans.  A strict cell has one exposed support exponent in each
active derivative row, and its matrices are the corresponding exponent rows
minus the coordinate unit row.  The admissibility hypothesis is not a hidden
leading-survival assumption: every reachable exposed face must satisfy the
following grouped private-tuple test.

For a face support E and P_E=sum_{alpha in E} c_alpha X^alpha, put

    h_ij(alpha) = alpha_i (alpha_j - delta_ij),

and expand

    det Hess(P_E)
      = sum_{(alpha_1,...,alpha_r) in E^r}
          (product_i c_{alpha_i}) D(alpha_1,...,alpha_r)
          X^(sum_i alpha_i - 2 one),

where D(alpha_1,...,alpha_r)=det[h_ij(alpha_i)].  A grouped private tuple
is a tuple with D nonzero such that no other row-labelled tuple with nonzero
D has the same exponent sum.  Permutations inside a single tuple are already
grouped in D; they are not incorrectly counted as different private terms.
The coefficient is required nonzero in K.  For a face all of whose exponents
are coordinatewise at least two, choose a generic secondary weight with a
unique minimizing alpha0.  The all-alpha0 tuple is then the unique lowest
secondary-weight group and has

    D(alpha0,...,alpha0)
      = (-1)^r (1-|alpha0|) product_i alpha0_i != 0,

so the private test is automatic in characteristic zero.  Faces with zero or
unit coordinates use the explicit grouped test instead.  This corrected
definition is the one used in the proof.

The support-derived theorem is quantified globally on the finite graph
reachable from a chosen cell: every forward edge and every Rstate-reflected
inverse edge must have strict selector/carry inequalities, target-cell
inclusion, and the private grouped-tuple property.  Define

    U_e = span_K { u : (u,w) is a positive integer seed in cell e },
    V_e = span_K { A_sigma u : (u,w) is a positive integer seed in cell e }.

For e=(sigma,tau,sigma-prime), the reflected inverse edge uses B[bar-tau]
on R u and A[bar-sigma-prime] on R v.  Exact phase reciprocity on the whole
reachable graph is equivalent to the two restrictions, on every reachable
edge,

    B[bar-tau] R u = R A[sigma] u       for u in U_e,
    A[bar-sigma-prime] R v = R B[tau] v for v in V_e,
    v = A[sigma] u.

When U_e and V_e are full, these are the full matrix identities.  The forward
state is (u,w) -> (B[tau]A[sigma]u,A[sigma]u); the inverse reflected state is
(Rw,Ru) -> (Rv,Ru-prime).  This fixes the component order and excludes a
same-seed assertion unless the pair is Rstate-fixed.  The converse is an
edge-by-edge linear-span argument, not a scalar total-degree argument.

### Canonical r=3 two-node support realization

Use R(1,2,3)=(3,2,1) and

    E_V={a1=(8,2,2), a2=(2,5,6), gamma=(2,8,2)},
    E_W={b1=R a1=(2,2,8), b2=R a2=(6,5,2)}.

Set A_i=one a_i^T-I and B_i=one b_i^T-I.  Explicitly,

    A1=[[7,2,2],[8,1,2],[8,2,1]],
    A2=[[1,5,6],[2,4,6],[2,5,5]],
    B1=[[1,2,8],[2,1,8],[2,2,7]],
    B2=[[5,5,2],[6,4,2],[6,5,1]].

Let K1 be the strict cone

    u>0,
    6u1-3u2-4u3>0,
    6u1-6u2>0,
    4u1-u2+8u3>0,

and K2 the strict cone

    u>0,
    -6u1+3u2+4u3>0,
    -3u2+4u3>0,
    -2u1+2u2+12u3>0,
    -2u1+8u2+6u3>0.

Define the actual full pair-state cells

    C_i^+ = { (u,w): u in K_i, w>0, A_i u - w >0 },
    C_i^- = Rstate(C_i^+),

with all inequalities componentwise.  These are open full-dimensional
subsets of R^6.  The first edge selects a1 then b2 and has

    C21=B2 A1=I+one(90,19,22),
    C21-I=one(90,19,22),
    A2 C21-A1=one(1074,231,268).

The target K2 score gaps are

    (a2-a1) dot C21 u=(84,22,26) dot u,
    (a2-gamma) dot C21 u=(90,16,26) dot u,
    (b2-b1) dot A2 C21 u=(1078,230,276) dot u,

so Phi maps C1-plus into C2-plus.  The second edge selects a2 then b2 and

    C22=B2 A2=I+one(18,55,70),
    A2 C22-A2=one(216,660,840).

Its score gaps after one step are

    (a2-a1) dot C22 u=(12,58,74) dot u,
    (a2-gamma) dot C22 u=(18,52,74) dot u,
    (b2-b1) dot A2 C22 u=(214,662,852) dot u,
    (a2-gamma) dot R A2 C22 u=(214,668,846) dot u.

Thus C2-plus maps into itself.  The pair carry is part of the same exact
calculation: A2 C21u>A1u and A2 C22u>A2u, while C21u>u and C22u>u.
Interior integer seeds are ((2,1,1),(1,1,1)) in C1-plus and
((1,1,1),(1,1,1)) in C2-plus.  The first produces A1u=(18,19,19) and
C21u=(223,222,222); the second produces A2u=(12,12,12) and
C22u=(144,144,144).  Normalize by the positive sum of all six coordinates
and take a sufficiently small rational closed neighborhood of either seed;
all listed strict forms then have a positive minimum margin.  Clearing
denominators supplies the required lattice seeds.

The reflected edge of C1-plus is B1 then A2, and the reflected edge of
C2-plus is B2 then A2.  They satisfy

    B1 R u=R A1 u,       A2 B1 R u=R C21 u,
    B2 R u=R A2 u,       A2 B2 R u=R C22 u.

The reflected carries are the R-images of the positive forward carries, so
C1-minus maps to C2-minus and C2-minus maps to itself.  Gamma is inactive on
all these forward and reflected phases; the four relevant strict forms are
the ones listed in K1/K2 and their R-images.  Yet gamma is an exposed vertex
on the open cone containing u=(1,10,1), where its score is 84 versus 30 and
58 for a1 and a2.  Since R gamma is absent from E_W, the full support pair is
not globally R-related.  This is a local reflection-closed component, not a
map-level reversibility claim.

The ordinary equal seed lies on a separate closed symmetry-wall stratum: all
three q weights are equal, a2 wins by total score, and C22 preserves the
equal ray.  It is intentionally not used to claim a transient strict-cell
orbit; the nonuniform integer seed above witnesses the two-node graph.

## E0024 disposition and all-face Hessian correction

E0024 is retained as historical prose but its machine block is non-authoritative
because the copied pre-manifest digest is malformed.  The next event supplies
the canonical digest.  It also closes two proof-display gaps.

First, the Hessian argument applies to every exposed face, not only singleton
strict chambers.  For a finite face F whose exponents are coordinatewise at
least two, choose a generic secondary linear form with a unique minimizer
alpha0 on F.  In the grouped determinant expansion, the tuple
(alpha0,...,alpha0) is the unique lowest secondary-weight tuple.  Its grouped
coefficient is

    (-1)^r (1-|alpha0|) product_i alpha0_i times c_alpha0^r,

which is nonzero in characteristic zero.  Any other tuple has larger
secondary weight and therefore a different exponent sum.  This proves the
private-transversal condition on vertices, edges, and the full triangle of
the displayed E_V support, and on both faces of E_W.  Boundary supports use
the explicitly grouped private-tuple test instead.

Second, the sharp cancellation fixture V=(q1+q2+q3)^3 and
W=(p1-p2)^3 loses its predicted leading W-gradient at the W half-step of
the first full application F^1: the three V leading p forms are equal, so
p1-p2 cancels and the W gradient has only the carried lower degree.  It is
not described as an n=2 full-iterate failure; it is a half-step obstruction
inside n=1 and is sufficient to show why the Hessian hypothesis is needed.

## v4 headline scope narrowed to positive mixed supports

To remove a row-face ambiguity rather than hide it in notation, the headline
theorem is now restricted to the positive mixed-support class

    E_V, E_W are subsets of Z_{≥2}^r, with r >= 3.

Every support monomial is active in every derivative row.  Hence each strict
normal-fan chamber has one common exposed vertex for the whole gradient, and
the selector is unambiguously A_alpha = one alpha-transpose minus I (and
similarly for W).  Strict vertex chambers are the theorem domain; tie/wall
faces are reported as excluded boundaries.  The grouped private-tuple lemma
still proves coefficient-uniform Hessian nonvanishing on every face and is
used for the sharp boundary discussion, but no row-wise sparse extension is
claimed in Paper 27.  This explicit r>=3 positive-support scope is the
canonical v4 headline and keeps P26's planar/zero-coordinate envelope theory
outside the claim.

The finite automaton is therefore completely support-derived: enumerate the
normal-fan chambers of the two Newton polytopes, retain chambers with strict
selector and carry inequalities, and certify each target inclusion by exact
rational cone implications.  Leading-form survival follows from the
positive-support Hessian lemma and injective substitution, not from an input
survival oracle.  On every edge of the closed reachable/reflected subgraph,
the two observable-span identities are required; the q and p spans are taken
over positive integer seeds in that edge cell.

The canonical C2 arithmetic is explicitly separated: the W selector gap is

    (b2-b1) dot A2 C22 u = (214,662,852) dot u,

whereas the target first-carry increment is the all-rows vector

    A2 C22 u - A2 u = one (216,660,840) dot u.

The reflected-gamma gap is (214,668,846) dot u.  These are three distinct
linear forms and no one is substituted for another.
