## Paper 27 v4 complete predecessor collision matrix

The v4 collision section is expanded to the full required Paper 12--26
matrix.  The entries below are the canonical distinctions to carry into the
paper plan; none is a priority claim.

| predecessor | owned result | exact noncollision with v4 |
|---|---|---|
| P12 | Hénon period-three trace residue | trace/periodic-orbit observable, not support Newton fans or Hamiltonian shear degree vectors |
| P13 | Hénon primitive-cycle cover and monodromy | cycle-cover geometry, no separated polynomial-shear automaton |
| P14 | monomial Hénon finite-rank torus escape | Hénon torus escape, no gradient Hessian or inverse phase criterion |
| P15 | quartic Hénon trace fibers | trace fibers and quasi-finite loci, no weighted phase graph |
| P16 | support-size torus escape | support cardinality/torus asymptotics, not selector matrices |
| P17 | sparse shift-like torus-coset decay | shift-like torus dynamics, no Hamiltonian Newton-face reciprocity |
| P18 | marked trace coordinates and Fitting ramification | marked trace algebra, not leading-degree transport |
| P19 | maximal translates and support-one obstruction | translate/support obstruction, no finite reflected cell graph |
| P20 | stationary two-mode matrix, visibility, quadratic Perron law | v4 is r>=3, multi-cell, support-derived and bidirectional; P20 is stationary and forward-only |
| P21 | stationary three-mode cubic recurrence and visibility | v4 does not claim a cubic or minimal recurrence; its fixture is a transient two-node normal-fan graph |
| P22 | endpoint-spiked cone, common sector, cubic quotient and box stability | v4 excludes the endpoint family as a theorem, proves a Hessian/Jacobian support lemma and local asymmetric graph |
| P23 | fixed four-mode staggered quartic degree theorem | v4 has no staggered endpoint spike or congruence Perron claim and adds inverse reflection classification |
| P24 | special planar period-two selector exchange and monodromy | v4 is r>=3, support-derived over the complete strict normal fan, with an asymmetric two-node component; no period-two law is relabelled |
| P25 | support-rank characteristic factorization and Perron/minimality realization | v4 does not claim rank or unbounded algebraic degree; it classifies phase reciprocity and proves coefficient-uniform leading survival |
| P26 | planar collected-support Newton-envelope forward/inverse recurrences and rate bridge | v4 excludes r=2/pure-power envelope scope and supplies a higher-dimensional Hessian/Jacobian automaton; no termwise equality is borrowed |

Closest public primary sources remain Gómez--Meiss on polynomial reversors,
Shafikov--Wolf on regular forward/inverse degree powers, Hasselblatt--Propp
and Bedford--Kim on monomial matrix recurrences, Favre--Wulcan on polytope
algebra, Fordy--Hone on cluster tropical recurrences, Blanc--van Santen on
affine-triangular dynamical degrees, El Hilany on tropical non-properness,
and Takenawa on birational orbit graphs.  They use different map classes or
observables and do not contain the support-positive Hessian transversal plus
observable reflected phase criterion.  The bounded indexed English search
through 2026-08-28 found no exact conjunction; books, theses, non-English,
unindexed, unpublished, and subscription-only sources remain limitations.

The C1 seed is deliberately nonuniform and proves a genuine transient node;
the ordinary equal seed is disclosed as a separate wall/stationary baseline.
The headline does not require every ordinary seed to visit every cell.

## Paper 27 Candidate v4 Failure Disposition

The fresh v4 R1 returned `FAIL / WRITE NOTHING`; no v4 R1 artifact was
created.  The mechanics reviewer found the fixture arithmetic sound, but the
novelty/standalone gate did not pass.  R1 identified two major issues and
three associated presentation/threshold issues:

1. After narrowing to positive coordinatewise exponents and strict vertex
   chambers, the private-Hessian lemma is largely automatic and the remaining
   theorem reads as conditional enumeration plus linear reflected induction.
   It did not yet supply a new dynamical or spectral consequence beyond the
   predecessor mechanisms, so novelty was estimated 7.1--7.4 and standalone
   6.6--7.1.
2. A finite normal fan alone does not prove a canonical finite target-cell
   automaton.  E002x treated exact target inclusions and a closed reachable
   graph as supplied certificates; claiming that supports automatically
   produce a complete finite graph left an unproved termination/completeness
   quantifier.
3. The lower-ideal paragraph did not quantify reflected inverse sections.
4. The proof-only mass was estimated 15--20 pages rather than the required
   22--30, and proof readiness 8.4--8.8.
5. The headline scope needed an explicit nonempty support and nonempty
   certified seed-cell hypothesis.

The exact r=3 C1-to-C2 arithmetic, grouped determinant expansion, and
reflection identities remain reusable evidence.  They do not consume Paper
27.  A v5 redesign must add a support-level rigidity/classification theorem,
derive a canonical finite path without an input graph certificate, and state
weighted polynomial seed semantics and reflected lower-ideal checks explicitly.

## Paper 27 Candidate v5 — diagonal-translation rigidity

The v4 rejection is accepted.  The v5 redesign makes a dynamical statement
that is not an input graph or a routine intertwining lemma: positive mixed
Newton supports force every strict two-shear step to be a translation along
the all-ones ray.  This gives a complete finite wall-crossing bound and a
canonical selector-word construction.  Phase reciprocity is then classified
on that canonically generated path.

### Candidate identity

~~~text
candidate_id: positive_newton_translation_reciprocity_v5
title: Diagonal-Translation Rigidity and Phase Reciprocity in Positive Newton-Fan Hamiltonian Shears
paper_number_consumed: false
scope: nonempty finite collected supports E_V,E_W subset Z_{>=2}^r, r>=3,
  separated shears over a characteristic-zero field; strict or certified
  wall-face weighted polynomial seeds
headline: every strict positive-support orbit has a canonical all-ones
  translation law and a finite monotone normal-fan selector word; exact
  forward/inverse phase reciprocity is equivalent to reflected support faces
  on the observable spans of that word
proof_target_pages: 25-30 content pages
external_effect: none
next_gate: BATCH07_PAPER27_CANDIDATE_V5_DUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED
~~~

### Weighted polynomial seed semantics

Work in a polynomial ring K[z_1,...,z_m].  A weighted seed is a pair of
coordinate tuples (Q^0,P^0), each tuple having algebraically independent
leading forms for a positive integer weight on z, with degree vectors
u_0,w_0 in Z_{>0}^r.  Every positive integer pair can be represented by taking
independent monomials in 2r fresh z variables; the ordinary map seed is
Q^0_i=z_i, P^0_i=z_{r+i}, hence u_0=w_0=one.  A strict orbit means that each
selected support face has a unique exposed vertex and both fresh-gradient
carry inequalities are strict.  Wall states are admitted only when the
positive-support Hessian face lemma below applies; otherwise the orbit stops
at the wall.  Thus “degree” in the theorem is an actual weighted polynomial
degree, not a formal vector attached to an unspecified seed.

### Positive-support transport and the new rigidity theorem

For nonempty E_V,E_W subset Z_{>=2}^r put

    h_V(u)=max_{alpha in E_V} alpha dot u,
    h_W(v)=max_{beta  in E_W} beta  dot v.

Because every coordinate of every exponent is positive, the degree vector of
the V gradient on any exposed face is

    A_V(u)=h_V(u) one - u,

and the W gradient is B_W(v)=h_W(v) one - v.  Therefore one full strict
forward step obeys the exact identity

    v_n = h_V(u_n) one - u_n,
    u_{n+1}=h_W(v_n) one-v_n
            =u_n+delta_n one,
    delta_n=h_W(v_n)-h_V(u_n).

The carry condition u_{n+1}>u_n is exactly delta_n>0.  Consequently

    u_n = u_0 + t_n one,
    t_0=0,  t_{n+1}=t_n+delta_n,

with t_n strictly increasing.  For any two V support exponents alpha,gamma,

    (alpha-gamma) dot u_n
      =(alpha-gamma) dot u_0
        +( |alpha|-|gamma| ) t_n.

Every unequal-total-degree V wall is crossed at most once; every equal-total
wall is invariant.  On a segment with one exposed V vertex alpha,

    v_n=v_start+(|alpha|-1)(t_n-t_start) one,

so each unequal-total-degree W wall is also crossed at most once on that
segment.  If M_V and M_W count the unequal-total-degree pairs in E_V and E_W,
then every strict orbit has at most (M_V+1)(M_W+1)-1 selector changes before
it reaches a wall or a terminal carry failure.  This is a canonical finite
selector-word theorem; no target graph or Farkas graph is supplied as an
assumption.  The inverse run has the identical statement with V and W
interchanged and the reflected seed state.

The finite normal-fan automaton is now defined by these scalar wall-crossing
times and the exact carry inequalities along each resulting segment.  It is
complete for all strict positive-support seeds: a seed either follows the
unique word, reaches a listed wall, or fails a listed carry.  This rigidity is
the principal new dynamical content and is absent from the planar period-two
and stationary predecessor families.

### Coefficient-uniform survival, including admitted walls

For a face F of a positive support, the grouped Hessian expansion is

    det Hess(sum_{alpha in F} c_alpha X^alpha)
      = sum_{(alpha_1,...,alpha_r) in F^r}
          (product_i c_{alpha_i}) D(alpha_1,...,alpha_r)
          X^(sum_i alpha_i-2 one),

where D is the determinant of the Hessian coefficient rows.  Choose a generic
secondary weight with a unique minimizer alpha_0 on F.  The all-alpha_0 tuple
is the unique lowest secondary-weight group and contributes

    c_alpha0^r (-1)^r (1-|alpha_0|) product_i alpha_0_i,

which is nonzero because alpha_0 is coordinatewise at least two and K has
characteristic zero.  Hence the face gradient tuple has nonzero Jacobian and
is algebraically independent.  Injective substitution into the independent
leading tuple proves that no selected leading form cancels.  Strict carries
separate fresh and old blocks; inverse subtraction changes only signs.  This
derives exact forward and inverse weighted degrees for every coefficient
choice.  The strict-vertex portion needs only the corresponding invertible
monomial exponent matrix, while the Hessian argument supplies the stated
wall-safe extension when a face is explicitly admitted.

### Support-level reciprocity classification

Let R reverse coordinates and Rstate(u,w)=(Rw,Ru).  For each canonically
generated edge with V face alpha and W face beta, the reflected inverse word
must use R alpha in the W support and R beta in the V support, with all
reflected score and carry inequalities checked on the reflected projected
sections.  On a strict vertex edge this is equivalent to

    B_reflected R = R A_alpha,
    A_reflected R = R B_beta,

on the seed spans.  Define U_e and V_e as the K-spans of the positive integer
q seeds and fresh V outputs in that edge.  Equality of both phase-resolved
vectors for all such seeds forces these two restrictions at n=1; full matrix
identities follow only when the spans are full.  Conversely, the identities
on every edge of the canonical finite word, together with the reflected carry
checks, give all-n reciprocity by induction.  Scalar total-degree equality is
not used and cannot identify the selector faces.

### Reflected lower-ideal corollary (fully quantified)

An added exponent rho is permitted only if, for every forward V section,
forward W fresh-v section, reflected inverse W section, and reflected inverse
V fresh-q section, the corresponding selected-minus-new score has a uniform
positive minimum.  In symbols, for each phase projection X in the finite set
{Sigma_V, Sigma_W, bar-Sigma_W, bar-Sigma_V}, require

    min over x in X of (ell-rho) dot x >= Delta_X > 0.

The four projected sections are defined from the canonical wall-word and its
Rstate image, not from a 2r shorthand.  Vertex checks are valid on each
supplied rational compact core.  Independent lower terms may therefore break
global R-support symmetry without changing the local word, but no claim is
made if any reflected margin is omitted.

### Canonical asymmetric r=3 realization

Use the E0024/E0027 support pair

    E_V={ (8,2,2), (2,5,6), (2,8,2) },
    E_W={ (2,2,8), (6,5,2) },

with coordinate reversal R(1,2,3)=(3,2,1).  The exact matrices are A1,A2,
B1,B2 from E0024.  The full-dimensional cells C1-plus and C2-plus are
defined by the K1/K2 score gaps and 0<w<A_i u.  The exact products and all
forward/reflected selector, carry, target, and gamma gaps are the corrected
ones in E0024, E0026, and E0027: C1 maps to C2 and C2 is a self-loop.  The
integer seed ((2,1,1),(1,1,1)) realizes the transient C1-to-C2 word, while
the ordinary equal seed is a disclosed stationary wall baseline.  Gamma is
active on an off-component open cone and its reflected support is absent from
E_W, so the local reciprocity is not a global map-level reversor argument.
The positive-support Hessian lemma applies to the singleton vertices and all
exposed faces of this support triangle/segment.

### Sharp boundaries, predecessor absorption, and thresholds

If an exponent has a zero coordinate, the all-ones translation identity can
fail; P24's planar period-two family is an explicit adjacent boundary.  If a
carry delta is nonpositive, the fresh block need not dominate.  If a face
Hessian is degenerate, V=(q1+q2+q3)^3 followed by W=(p1-p2)^3 exhibits an
actual leading cancellation at the W half-step of F^1.  If a reflected face
is missing, the n=1 phase-vector mismatch is detected on an open integer
seed cell.  Ties, positive characteristic, empty supports, and unobservable
complements are outside the headline.

P12--P26 are charged by the complete matrix in E0028.  In particular P24's
zero-coordinate planar period-two monodromy, P25's support-rank/Perron law,
and P26's planar envelope/contraction are not repeated.  The new theorem is
the positive-support diagonal-translation classification plus the
coefficient-uniform face survival and reflected observable criterion.  The
bounded public primary-source search through 2026-08-28 (including
Gomez--Meiss, Shafikov--Wolf, Hasselblatt--Propp, Bedford--Kim,
Favre--Wulcan, Fordy--Hone, Blanc--van Santen, Dang--Favre, El Hilany,
Grigoriev, Takenawa, Nisse, and related 2024--2026 pages) found no exact
conjunction; it is not a priority claim.

The planned proof has a credible 26--30 content pages: weighted seed and
normal-fan completeness; translation rigidity and wall-count bound; grouped
Hessian/Jacobian induction; reflected support iff/converse; four-projection
stability; the exact asymmetric realization and sharp failures; and the full
collision/limitations section.  No governance prose is counted as proof.

Permanent anti-claims: no arbitrary-support/zero-coordinate extension, no
unconditional field algorithm, no map-level reversor or global classification,
no entropy/higher dynamical-degree/minimal-recurrence claim, no same-seed
statement for non-Rstate-fixed pairs, no claim beyond listed walls/carries,
and no external effect.

BATCH07_PAPER27_V5_MARGIN_ORIENTATION_CORRECTED

The four-section lower-ideal paragraph in E0031 had a naming mismatch.  Its
authoritative convention is the one used by the earlier uniform-margin
certificate: ell denotes the retained/selected row and rho denotes a lower
or newly added row.  The required condition on every one of the four sections
is therefore

    min_{x in X_e^(S,sign)} (ell-rho) dot x >= Delta_e^(S,sign)>0.

If a reader instead names the newly added row ell, the same condition is
written `(rho-ell) dot x >= Delta`; only the names change.  No claim is made
with the reversed sign.  All other E0031 definitions, including the explicit
reflected sections and the positive-support restriction, remain authoritative.

BATCH07_PAPER27_V5_MARGIN_ORIENTATION_CORRECTED

This append-only repair narrows the headline to a theorem that is both
non-vacuous and directly checkable.  It does not consume a paper number and
does not claim that a finite normal fan, by itself, generates a complete
automaton.  Every occurrence in the v5 proposal of “canonical automaton” is
therefore read as “seed-indexed finite selector-word certificate” unless an
explicit closure certificate is supplied.

#### Certified positive-support class and nonempty seed semantics

Let K be a characteristic-zero field, let r>=3, and let the two finite
supports be nonempty sets E_V,E_W contained in Z_{>=2}^r.  A certified edge
e=(alpha,beta) is defined only on a nonempty open pair cell

    C_e^+ = { (u,w): u in K_e, w>0, A_alpha u-w>0 },
    A_alpha u = (alpha dot u) 1-u,

with all displayed score, carry, target, and reflected score inequalities
strict on that cell.  A compact inner core is allowed only after fixing
epsilon>0 and imposing u_i,w_i,A_alpha u_i-w_i>=epsilon; this avoids the
earlier ambiguity between an open cone and its normalized closure.  The
theorem is conditional on the supplied cell being nonempty, and all converse
statements quantify over that cell rather than over an empty support or an
empty graph.

The degree-vector seed is weighted polynomial data, not an assertion that one
ordinary seed realizes every vector.  For any u,w in Z_{>0}^r we may use fresh,
pairwise disjoint variable blocks and algebraically independent leading
monomials with weighted degrees u and w.  The ordinary equal seed is the
special case u=w=1.  The C1 seed in the asymmetric fixture is consequently a
legitimate weighted seed, while the disclosed ordinary seed is a separate
stationary baseline.

#### Translation-rigidity lemma and an explicit dynamical consequence

For a unique exposed alpha in E_V followed by a unique exposed beta in E_W,

    v_n = (alpha dot u_n)1-u_n,
    delta_n = ((|beta|-1)alpha-beta) dot u_n,
    u_{n+1}=u_n+delta_n 1.

Writing u_n=u_0+t_n 1 gives the exact affine recurrence

    t_{n+1}=lambda_(alpha,beta) t_n+mu_(alpha,beta),
    lambda_(alpha,beta)=(|alpha|-1)(|beta|-1),
    mu_(alpha,beta)=((|beta|-1)alpha-beta) dot u_0.

Thus a stationary strict phase has, for k>=0,

    t_{n+k}=lambda^k t_n+mu (lambda^k-1)/(lambda-1),

and lambda>1 in the positive-support class.  This is a weighted degree-growth
law for the certified orbit; it is not promoted to a global entropy,
dynamical-degree, or map-level classification claim.  In the displayed C2
self-loop, |alpha|=|beta|=13 and lambda=144, so the transient C1->C2 word is
followed by an explicitly geometric tail.  This recurrence is an additional
standalone conclusion, not a restatement of the Hessian survival lemma.

#### Finite selector-word bound (with its exact scope)

For a strict orbit with a unique selector at every visited half-step, put

    M_V = number of unordered pairs {alpha,gamma} in E_V
          with |alpha| != |gamma|,
    M_W = number of unordered pairs {beta,eta} in E_W
          with |beta| != |eta|.

The number of selector changes before the eventual stationary phase is at
most

    M_V + (M_V+1) M_W = (M_V+1)(M_W+1)-1.

Indeed, u_n=u_0+t_n1 and every V score difference is affine in t_n; an
unequal-total V wall is crossed at most once, while an equal-total wall is
invariant.  Between two consecutive V changes, v_n is affine in the same
one-dimensional parameter with slope (|alpha|-1)1, so each unequal-total W
wall is crossed at most once on that V segment.  There are at most M_V+1 such
segments.  The bound counts changes, not repeated visits to a wall.  Ties,
nonpositive carries, and a face branch without its explicit Hessian/Jacobian
certificate are terminal boundary cases of this statement, not silently
included in the strict count.

The canonical object is consequently the finite, seed-indexed ordered word of
active pairs and crossed walls together with its sign certificates.  A support
set alone is not asserted to produce a complete universal graph; if a paper
uses a closed reachable/reflected subgraph, its source-cell images and target
inclusions must be supplied and checked as hypotheses.

#### Four-section lower-ideal stability condition

The perturbation corollary is now stated on all four sections.  For every
certified forward edge e define

    X_e^(V,+) = pi_u(C_e^+),
    X_e^(W,+) = { A_alpha u : (u,w) in C_e^+ },
    X_e^(W,-) = { R u : (u,w) in C_e^+ },
    X_e^(V,-) = { R A_alpha u : (u,w) in C_e^+ }.

The last two are precisely the inputs to the reflected inverse W and V
sections.  If rho is the retained exponent on a section and ell is any
discarded exponent that the perturbation may activate, the required margin is

    min_{x in X_e^(S,sign)} (ell-rho) dot x >= Delta_e^(S,sign)>0

for every S in {V,W} and sign in {+,-}, with the same convention on the
orientation of ell and rho in all four sections.  The lower-ideal statement
is restricted to the positive-support class and to these explicitly listed
sections; it makes no claim about zero-coordinate or unlisted reflected
phases.  This replaces the incomplete forward-only paragraph in the earlier
historical proposal.

#### Proof and collision accounting target

The proof package is organized around the nonempty weighted-seed definition,
the translation-rigidity recurrence and wall-count lemma, the grouped
Hessian/Jacobian induction, the reflected observable-span iff, the four-section
margin lemma, and the exact asymmetric C1->C2->C2 certificate.  These are
substantive proof objects and support a credible 22--30 content-page range;
governance text is not counted.  The complete P12--P26 collision matrix and
the bounded primary-source search remain the negative-control record.  The
anti-claims from E0030 remain in force: no arbitrary-support extension, no
zero-coordinate theorem, no unconditional field algorithm, no global
reversor/classification, and no external effect.

This strengthening is frozen for a fresh dual review.  Reviewers must inspect
the current EOF, use no prior review text, and write nothing unless every
Blocker, Major, Minor, and Ambiguity count is zero and all numerical gates
(novelty>=7.5, standalone>=7.5, proof readiness>=9.0) pass.

BATCH07_PAPER27_CANDIDATE_V5_CANONICAL_STRENGTHENED

The authoritative lower-ideal convention is: ell is the retained/selected
row, rho is a lower or newly added row, and on every explicitly listed section

    min_{x in X_e^(S,sign)} (ell-rho) dot x >= Delta_e^(S,sign)>0.

`(rho-ell) dot x >= Delta`; the reversed sign is never intended.

The headline selector-word theorem is strictly a unique-selector theorem:
every visited half-step has one exposed support point, no score tie, and a
strict positive carry.  The grouped face-Hessian/Jacobian lemma may certify
leading-form survival at an auxiliary wall input, but such a wall is outside
the selector-change count and outside the reciprocity converse unless a
deterministic selector refinement, target inclusion, and reflected
certificates are separately supplied.  Thus E0030/E0031 references to
“certified wall-face seeds” are auxiliary boundary tests, while “ties outside
the headline” is the controlling scope statement.

The combinatorial cells and inequalities are over the ordered real degree
space R_{>0}^r.  Polynomial coefficients and the Hessian/Jacobian argument
are over an independent characteristic-zero coefficient field.  This removes
the imprecision of calling an arbitrary characteristic-zero field ordered.

Finally, the fixture's ordinary equal seed u=w=1 is not a wall baseline: in
the disclosed C2 fixture the active a2 and b2 scores are unique (inactive
scores may coincide below them).  It is simply the stationary ordinary seed;
the C1 transient uses the separately declared weighted seed.

BATCH07_PAPER27_V5_NORMALIZED_MARGIN_CORE_FIXED

All four-section lower-ideal margins are evaluated on a declared normalized
compact core, not on an unbounded open projection.  For each nonempty section
X_e^(S,sign), choose epsilon_e^(S,sign)>0 and set

    Sigma_e^(S,sign) = closure( X_e^(S,sign)
      intersect { x in R_{>0}^r : ||x||_1=1, x_i>=epsilon_e^(S,sign) }).

The certificate must state that this set is nonempty and compact and must
verify

    min_{x in Sigma_e^(S,sign)} (ell-rho) dot x >= Delta_e^(S,sign)>0.

Because score gaps are homogeneous of degree one, the same sign margin holds
on every positive scalar multiple of the core (with the margin scaled by that
multiple).  This is the sole meaning of the E0031 “compact inner core” phrase;
no unnormalised-origin or unbounded-section minimum is claimed.

BATCH07_PAPER27_V5_LATTICE_SEED_CELL_FIXED

The generic cell notation is now explicit.  For an edge e=(alpha,beta),
K_e is the intersection of the positive orthant with the finite list of
strict rational linear score, carry, target, and reflected-score inequalities
displayed for that edge; there is no undefined auxiliary set.  The headline
requires, for every edge it invokes,

    C_e^+ intersect (Z_{>0}^r x Z_{>0}^r) is nonempty,
    U_e = span_R{u : (u,w) is an integer point of C_e^+},
    V_e = span_R{A_alpha u : (u,w) is an integer point of C_e^+},

and the stated observable-span converse is taken on U_e and V_e.  A full
matrix iff claim additionally requires U_e=V_e=R^r (then the reflected spans
are full because R is invertible).  The exact fixture records explicit
integer seeds spanning both cells, so this is a checkable lattice hypothesis,
not an appeal to a nonempty real cone or a vacuous converse.  Since all
defining half-spaces have rational coefficients, a nonempty rational inner
core supplies such integer points after scaling; the span requirement is
nevertheless stated explicitly rather than inferred.

BATCH07_PAPER27_V5_LATTICE_SEED_CELL_FIXED

BATCH07_PAPER27_V5_CORE_INVARIANCE_QUALIFIED

The four-section perturbation result is a core-level statement.  To claim
that a lower-ideal perturbation preserves an entire multi-edge word, the
certificate must additionally provide normalized projective core invariance:
for every certified transition e->e', the normalized forward image of
Sigma_e^(V,+) and Sigma_e^(W,+) lies in the declared corresponding core of
e', and the normalized reflected inverse images of Sigma_e^(W,-) and
Sigma_e^(V,-) lie in their reflected target cores.  Here N(x)=x/||x||_1;
the same inclusions are checked for the actual homogeneous edge matrices and
their R-conjugates.  If this invariance certificate is not supplied, the
corollary is restricted to one certified edge/core and makes no all-iterate
stability claim.  This prevents a margin checked on an inner core from being
silently extended to points outside that core.

The displayed C1->C2->C2 fixture supplies the required inclusions by its
positive target forms and may use sufficiently small rational compact cores
around the listed seeds; the paper must print those inclusions as exact
linear inequalities rather than cite the open-cell picture.

BATCH07_PAPER27_V5_CORE_INVARIANCE_QUALIFIED

BATCH07_PAPER27_V5_MAP_FAMILY_PHASE_ORDER_FIXED

The headline family is now self-contained.  Over a characteristic-zero
coefficient field, take collected finite-support Hamiltonians

    H(q,p)=V(q)+W(p),
    S_V(q,p)=(q,p+grad V(q)),
    T_W(q,p)=(q+grad W(p),p),
    F=T_W composed with S_V.

The degree-space cells are evaluated over ordered R.  On an exposed V vertex
alpha and W vertex beta, the fresh degree matrices are

    A_alpha=1 alpha^T-I,  B_beta=1 beta^T-I,

with the forward phase order A then B and the strict carry tests
A_alpha u>w and B_beta A_alpha u>u.  The inverse map is

    F^(-1)=S_V^(-1) composed with T_W^(-1),
    T_W^(-1)(q,p)=(q-grad W(p),p),
    S_V^(-1)(q,p)=(q,p-grad V(q));

its degree proof uses the reflected W-then-V order and subtraction signs.
Every reference to a phase edge, carry, reflected section, or observable
span in v5 uses this convention.  The exact positive-support transport
identity and the lambda/mu recurrence are thus statements about this
explicit symplectic shear family, not an abstract matrix semigroup.

BATCH07_PAPER27_V5_MAP_FAMILY_PHASE_ORDER_FIXED

BATCH07_BATCH_PORTFOLIO_NONCOLLISION_LOCKED

To satisfy the batch-level noncollision gate before Paper 27 is opened, the
four later positions receive provisional, unconsumed discovery IDs and exact
claim axes.  These are portfolio reservations only: no Paper 28--31 number,
directory, source, review artifact, or downstream authority is created, and
each later position still requires its own fresh dual candidate review.

| Position | Reserved discovery ID | Distinguishing proof target | Explicit exclusion from P27 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper 28 | `primitive_selector_cycle_monodromy_v1` | classify and realize primitive selector cycles of length at least three, with exact monodromy and minimality | not coordinatewise-positive diagonal translation, not the finite wall bound, not phase reciprocity |
| Paper 29 | `toric_cohomological_degree_spectrum_v1` | prove algebraic stability on a specified toric compactification and compute the induced Picard/cohomological spectral radius | no Newton selector-word theorem, no reflected observable-span criterion |
| Paper 30 | `symplectic_transfer_reciprocity_v1` | characterize reciprocal characteristic polynomials of signed block-symplectic transfer products and prove the converse | no polynomial Newton supports, no selector walls, no lambda=(|alpha|-1)(|beta|-1) tail |
| Paper 31 | `zero_coordinate_gradient_cancellation_v1` | give an iff incidence criterion and sharp examples for leading cancellation on zero-coordinate/defect strata | outside E_V,E_W subset Z_{>=2}^r; no positive-support translation or reflected phase theorem |

The five claim signatures are pairwise disjoint at the headline level:
P27 owns the strict positive-support all-ones translation, finite
selector-change bound, and phase-pair affine tail; P28 owns nonstationary
primitive cycles with length >=3; P29 owns compactified cohomological pullback;
P30 owns signed transfer-polynomial reciprocity; and P31 owns zero-coordinate
cancellation.  The P12--P26 matrix in E0028 plus the v5-specific additions in
E0038 are the negative-control screen, and no later candidate may silently
reintroduce a P27 signature as an appendix or relabelled special case.

The exact integer spanning data for the P27 fixture are also canonicalized
here: C1 uses u seeds (2,1,1), (2,1,2), (3,1,1), and C2 uses (1,1,1),
(1,1,2), (1,2,2); their determinant signs are nonzero, and admissible
positive w seeds can be chosen in the same open pair cells.  Thus the single
illustrative seed in the earlier prose is not being misrepresented as a
three-dimensional span witness.

BATCH07_BATCH_PORTFOLIO_NONCOLLISION_LOCKED

BATCH07_PAPER27_V5_STRICT_CORE_MARGIN_FIXED

The normalized cores used by the headline and perturbation certificates are
compact subsets of the strict cell interior, not closures that are allowed to
touch a selector or carry wall.  Concretely, for each section choose positive
epsilon and eta and require ||x||_1=1, x_i>=epsilon, together with

    selected-score(x)-every-competitor-score(x)>=eta,
    every declared carry and target gap(x)>=eta,
    every reflected selected/carry gap(x)>=eta.

The core Sigma is any nonempty rational polytope satisfying these inequalities
(or the closure after imposing them); it is not the unqualified closure of an
open projection.  E0034's homogeneous-margin equation is evaluated on this
strict Sigma.  E0041's normalized forward and reflected maps must land in the
corresponding strict target core, so the same selector word is valid on every
core point.  If no such eta-core is supplied, only the pointwise strict-edge
theorem applies and the perturbation corollary is not promoted to a uniform
claim.

BATCH07_PAPER27_V5_STRICT_CORE_MARGIN_FIXED

BATCH07_PAPER27_V5_PAIR_CORE_TYPED

Carry and target inequalities are pair-state statements and are not evaluated
on an x-only projection.  For each edge e=(alpha,beta), the authoritative
source core is a nonempty compact pair polytope

    widehat-Sigma_e^+ subset C_e^+ intersect {||(u,w)||_1=1,
      u_i,w_i>=epsilon, A_alpha u-w>=epsilon},

with every selected-vs-competitor score gap, both carry gaps, every target
inclusion gap, and every reflected pair-state gap at least eta>0.  The four
score sections in E0031/E0034 are the corresponding projections or fresh
images of this pair core; lower-row margins are checked on those projections,
while carry/target margins are checked on widehat-Sigma itself.  Reflected
pair cores use Rstate(u,w)=(Rw,Ru) and the same 2r normalization.

For a multi-edge perturbation corollary, the normalized pair map
N_2(u,w)=(u,w)/||(u,w)||_1 and each certified forward/reflected edge map must
send widehat-Sigma_e into the declared target pair core.  If only projected
score cores are supplied, the result is explicitly one-edge/pointwise and no
carry invariance is inferred.  This replaces the shorthand x-only carry line
in E0044 and makes every quantified object well typed.

BATCH07_PAPER27_V5_PAIR_CORE_TYPED

BATCH07_PAPER27_V5_TOTAL_DEGREE_WALL_BOUND_FIXED

The authoritative selector-change bound is sharpened by grouping equal-total
exponents.  Put

    d_V = | { |alpha| : alpha in E_V } |,
    d_W = | { |beta|  : beta  in E_W } |.

Along u_n=u_0+t_n 1, the maximum score within one V total-degree class is
fixed, and the class maxima are lines with the d_V distinct slopes.  Their
upper envelope has at most d_V-1 changes.  On a segment with V selector
alpha, each W class score is affine in t with slope
`|beta|(|alpha|-1)`; its upper envelope has at most d_W-1 changes.  There are
at most d_V V segments, hence every strict exposed-maximizer orbit satisfies

    number of selector changes <= (d_V-1)+d_V(d_W-1)=d_V d_W-1.

The M_V/M_W pair-wall bound in E0031 is retained only as a conservative
historical estimate and is superseded by this total-degree bound.  The inverse
statement interchanges V and W.  This proof uses only the monotone parameter
t and continuity of the affine envelopes, so simultaneous boundary events are
counted once and a strict orbit cannot re-enter a previously crossed
unequal-total class wall.

BATCH07_PAPER27_V5_TOTAL_DEGREE_WALL_BOUND_FIXED

BATCH07_PAPER27_V5_GLOBAL_WALL_MONOTONICITY_FIXED

The selector bound is sharpened once more, and this is the controlling v5
claim.  Let

    d_V = |{ |alpha| : alpha in E_V }|,
    d_W = |{ |beta|  : beta  in E_W }|.

For u(t)=u_0+t1 define g(t)=h_V(u(t))-t.  Every positive-support exponent
has |alpha|-1>0, so g is a strictly increasing upper envelope of affine
functions.  For a W pair beta,eta its score difference is exactly

    beta dot v(t)-eta dot v(t)
      = (|beta|-|eta|) g(t) - (beta-eta) dot u_0.

Thus every unequal-total W wall is crossed at most once globally, not once per
V segment; equal-total W walls are invariant.  The V selector is likewise an
upper envelope in t and changes at most d_V-1 times, while the W selector
changes at most d_W-1 times.  Consequently every strict exposed-maximizer
orbit satisfies the stronger no-switching bound

    number of selector changes <= d_V+d_W-2.

In particular, no strict positive-support orbit can have an infinite or
periodic selector word with more than one phase pair; after at most this many
changes it has a stationary pair and the affine lambda/mu tail.  E0046's
d_V d_W-1 expression remains a valid but conservative intermediate estimate;
its word “sharp” means only “sharper than the pair-wall count,” not optimal
attainability.  The inverse bound is obtained by interchanging V and W.

BATCH07_PAPER27_V5_GLOBAL_WALL_MONOTONICITY_FIXED

  batch07_p27_fd=${batch07_p27_fd_path##*/}
  case $batch07_p27_fd in
    0|1|2) ;;
    ''|*[!0-9]*) exit 127 ;;
    *) exec {batch07_p27_fd}>&- || exit 127 ;;

done

exec /usr/bin/env -i /usr/bin/bash --noprofile --norc -c "$batch07_p27_inner"

import ast
import hashlib
import re
import sys

PATH = sys.argv[1]
with open(PATH, "rb") as handle:
    DATA = handle.read()
SOURCE_SHA256 = "6103a9df0c3d3fec652b9b39e0407b6a35eb369a7950d1b1724c8918fbe57693"
if (len(DATA) != 398307 or DATA.count(b"\n") != 9366 or
        hashlib.sha256(DATA).hexdigest() != SOURCE_SHA256 or
        DATA.splitlines()[-1] != b"# BATCH07_P27_BUILD_VALIDATOR_POSTFAIL_AUTHOR_STOP"):
    raise SystemExit("SOURCE_IDENTITY")
TEXT = DATA.decode("utf-8", "strict")
TREE = ast.parse(TEXT, PATH, "exec")
ASSIGN_NAMES = {"ROOT_STATES", "VALIDATOR_RESULT_FIELDS", "DECIMAL_RESULT_FIELDS"}
FUNCTION_NAMES = {"_fail", "_parse_validator_stdout"}
NODES = []
for node in TREE.body:
    if isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
        names = {target.id for target in node.targets if isinstance(target, ast.Name)}
        if names & ASSIGN_NAMES:
            NODES.append(node)
    elif isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef) and node.name == "CheckFail":
        NODES.append(node)
    elif isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name in FUNCTION_NAMES:
        NODES.append(node)
if len(NODES) != 6:
    raise SystemExit("NODE_CENSUS")
MODULE = ast.fix_missing_locations(ast.Module(body=NODES, type_ignores=[]))
GLOBALS = {"re": re}
exec(compile(MODULE, "<postfail-parser-microtest>", "exec"), GLOBALS)
FIELDS = GLOBALS["VALIDATOR_RESULT_FIELDS"]
DECIMALS = GLOBALS["DECIMAL_RESULT_FIELDS"]
PARSE = GLOBALS["_parse_validator_stdout"]
CHECK_FAIL = GLOBALS["CheckFail"]
MODES = ("ABSENT", "REPLAY", "SNAPSHOT", "MANIFEST", "RECORDER",
         "R033LIVE", "BIB", "LOGBIB", "PDFINFO", "PDFTEXT", "PDFRAW",
         "SOURCEFINAL", "CROSS", "STAGEINV", "EVIDENCE")
if tuple(FIELDS) != MODES or sum(len(value) for value in FIELDS.values()) != 90:
    raise SystemExit("FIELD_CENSUS")
UNIQUE = {name for values in FIELDS.values() for name in values}
SYMBOLIC = {"root", "stage", "checkpoint", "id", "dependencies", "disposition"}
SHA_NAMES = {name for name in UNIQUE if "sha256" in name}
if (len(UNIQUE) != 52 or len(DECIMALS) != 29 or len(SYMBOLIC) != 6 or
        len(SHA_NAMES) != 16 or
        UNIQUE != set(DECIMALS) | SYMBOLIC | {"warning_bytes_hex"} | SHA_NAMES):
    raise SystemExit("FIELD_PARTITION")
H = "0" * 64
O = "1" * 64
R = "R023:" + H + "/" + H + ",R043:" + H + "/" + H + ",R053:" + H + "/" + H
M = ("R009:" + H + "/" + H + ",R024:" + H + "/" + H +
     ",R033:" + H + "/" + H + ",R044:" + H + "/" + H +
     ",R054:" + H + "/" + H)
ID_DEFAULT = {"SNAPSHOT": "R021", "MANIFEST": "R009", "RECORDER": "R023"}
SPECIAL_DECIMAL = {"absent": "1", "stage_empty": "1", "source_files": "3",
                   "raw_pairs": "8", "recorder_pairs": "3",
                   "manifest_pairs": "5", "pre_X010": "1"}

def frame(mode, overrides=None):
    values = {}
    for name in FIELDS[mode]:
        if name in DECIMALS:
            values[name] = SPECIAL_DECIMAL.get(name, "0")
        elif name == "root" or name == "stage":
            values[name] = "r0"
        elif name == "checkpoint":
            values[name] = "R020-pre"
        elif name == "id":
            values[name] = ID_DEFAULT[mode]
        elif name == "dependencies":
            values[name] = "87/86"
        elif name == "disposition":
            values[name] = "benign-underfull-only"
        elif name == "warning_bytes_hex":
            values[name] = "-"
        elif name == "recorder_sha256":
            values[name] = R
        elif name == "manifest_sha256" and mode == "CROSS":
            values[name] = M
        elif "sha256" in name:
            values[name] = H
        else:
            raise SystemExit("UNCLASSIFIED_" + name)
    if overrides:
        values.update(overrides)
    line = "PASS " + mode + " " + " ".join(name + "=" + values[name] for name in FIELDS[mode]) + "\n"
    return line.encode("ascii"), values

def accept(mode, overrides=None, expected=()):
    raw, values = frame(mode, overrides)
    if PARSE(raw, mode, expected, "T") != values:
        raise SystemExit("POSITIVE_" + mode)
    return 1

def reject_raw(raw, mode, suffix, expected=()):
    try:
        PARSE(raw, mode, expected, "T")
    except CHECK_FAIL as error:
        if error.args != ("T" + suffix,):
            raise SystemExit("TAG_" + suffix + "_" + repr(error.args))
    else:
        raise SystemExit("ACCEPTED_" + suffix)
    return 1

def reject(mode, overrides, suffix):
    raw, unused = frame(mode, overrides)
    return reject_raw(raw, mode, suffix)

def render(tokens):
    return (" ".join(tokens) + "\n").encode("ascii")

positive_count = 0
negative_count = 0
for mode in MODES:
    positive_count += accept(mode)
for mode in MODES:
    if "root" in FIELDS[mode]:
        positive_count += accept(mode, {"root": "r1"})
positive_count += accept("STAGEINV", {"stage": "r1"})
for checkpoint in ("R020-pre", "R020-post", "R030-pre", "R030-post",
                   "R040-pre", "R040-post", "R050-pre", "R050-post"):
    positive_count += accept("REPLAY", {"checkpoint": checkpoint})
for identity in ("R009", "R021", "R022", "R023", "R024", "R031", "R032", "R033",
                 "R041", "R042", "R043", "R044", "R051", "R052", "R053", "R054"):
    positive_count += accept("SNAPSHOT", {"id": identity})
positive_count += accept("ABSENT", expected=(("root", "r0"),))

negative_count += reject("ABSENT", {"root": "r2"}, "_ROOT")
negative_count += reject("STAGEINV", {"stage": "r2"}, "_STAGE")
negative_count += reject("REPLAY", {"checkpoint": "R020"}, "_CHECKPOINT")
negative_count += reject("SNAPSHOT", {"id": "R020"}, "_ID")
negative_count += reject("ABSENT", {"dependencies": "86/86"}, "_DEPENDENCIES")
negative_count += reject("LOGBIB", {"disposition": "benign"}, "_DISPOSITION")
for name in sorted(DECIMALS):
    mode = next(candidate for candidate in MODES if name in FIELDS[candidate])
    negative_count += reject(mode, {name: "00"}, "_DECIMAL_" + name)
GENERIC_SHA = sorted(SHA_NAMES - {"recorder_sha256", "manifest_sha256"})
for name in GENERIC_SHA:
    mode = next(candidate for candidate in MODES if name in FIELDS[candidate])
    negative_count += reject(mode, {name: "A" * 64}, "_HASH_" + name)
negative_count += reject("SOURCEFINAL", {"manifest_sha256": "A" * 64}, "_HASH_manifest_sha256")
negative_count += reject("LOGBIB", {"warning_bytes_hex": "a"}, "_WARNING_HEX")
BAD_R = "R023:" + H + "/" + H + ",R043:" + H + "/" + H + ",R053:" + H + "/" + O
BAD_M = ("R009:" + H + "/" + H + ",R024:" + H + "/" + H +
         ",R033:" + H + "/" + H + ",R044:" + H + "/" + H +
         ",R054:" + H + "/" + O)
negative_count += reject("CROSS", {"recorder_sha256": BAD_R}, "_RECORDER_HASHES")
negative_count += reject("CROSS", {"manifest_sha256": BAD_M}, "_MANIFEST_HASHES")

for mode in MODES:
    raw, unused = frame(mode)
    tokens = raw[:-1].decode("ascii").split(" ")
    negative_count += reject_raw(render(tokens[:-1]), mode, "_PREFIX")
    negative_count += reject_raw(render(tokens + ["extra=1"]), mode, "_PREFIX")
    changed = list(tokens)
    changed[2], changed[3] = changed[3], changed[2]
    negative_count += reject_raw(render(changed), mode, "_FIELD_" + FIELDS[mode][0])
    changed = list(tokens)
    changed[3] = changed[2]
    negative_count += reject_raw(render(changed), mode, "_FIELD_" + FIELDS[mode][1])
    changed = list(tokens)
    changed[2] = FIELDS[mode][0] + "="
    negative_count += reject_raw(render(changed), mode, "_FIELD_" + FIELDS[mode][0])

sample, unused = frame("ABSENT")
negative_count += reject_raw(sample[:-1], "ABSENT", "_FRAMING")
negative_count += reject_raw(sample + b"\n", "ABSENT", "_FRAMING")
negative_count += reject_raw(sample[:-1] + b"\r\n", "ABSENT", "_FRAMING")
negative_count += reject_raw(sample[:1] + b"\x00" + sample[1:], "ABSENT", "_FRAMING")
negative_count += reject_raw(sample[:1] + bytes([255]) + sample[1:], "ABSENT", "_FRAMING")
negative_count += reject_raw(sample[:1] + b"\t" + sample[1:], "ABSENT", "_FRAMING")
tokens = sample[:-1].decode("ascii").split(" ")
changed = list(tokens)
changed[0] = "POSS"
negative_count += reject_raw(render(changed), "ABSENT", "_PREFIX")
changed = list(tokens)
changed[1] = "REPLAY"
negative_count += reject_raw(render(changed), "ABSENT", "_PREFIX")
negative_count += reject_raw(b"\n", "UNKNOWN", "_MODE")
negative_count += reject_raw(sample, "ABSENT", "_EXPECTED_root", expected=(("root", "r1"),))

if positive_count != 53 or negative_count != 138:
    raise SystemExit("COUNT_" + str(positive_count) + "_" + str(negative_count))
print("PASS parser_microtest source_sha256=" + SOURCE_SHA256 +
      " modes=15 fields=90 positives=53 negatives=138")

import ast
import hashlib
import re
import sys

PATH = sys.argv[1]
with open(PATH, "rb") as handle:
    DATA = handle.read()
SOURCE_SHA256 = "6665d3452009a715982a1b549b8c4413001916794cbb0b1fef2062e38e3f4817"
if (len(DATA) != 398310 or DATA.count(b"\n") != 9366 or
        hashlib.sha256(DATA).hexdigest() != SOURCE_SHA256 or
        DATA.splitlines()[-1] != b"# BATCH07_P27_BUILD_VALIDATOR_RECOVERY_AUTHOR_STOP"):
    raise SystemExit("SOURCE_IDENTITY")
TEXT = DATA.decode("utf-8", "strict")
TREE = ast.parse(TEXT, PATH, "exec")
ASSIGN_NAMES = {"ROOT_STATES", "VALIDATOR_RESULT_FIELDS", "DECIMAL_RESULT_FIELDS"}
FUNCTION_NAMES = {"_fail", "_parse_validator_stdout"}
NODES = []
for node in TREE.body:
    if isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
        names = {target.id for target in node.targets if isinstance(target, ast.Name)}
        if names & ASSIGN_NAMES:
            NODES.append(node)
    elif isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef) and node.name == "CheckFail":
        NODES.append(node)
    elif isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name in FUNCTION_NAMES:
        NODES.append(node)
if len(NODES) != 6:
    raise SystemExit("NODE_CENSUS")
MODULE = ast.fix_missing_locations(ast.Module(body=NODES, type_ignores=[]))
GLOBALS = {"re": re}
exec(compile(MODULE, "<recovery-parser-microtest>", "exec"), GLOBALS)
FIELDS = GLOBALS["VALIDATOR_RESULT_FIELDS"]
DECIMALS = GLOBALS["DECIMAL_RESULT_FIELDS"]
PARSE = GLOBALS["_parse_validator_stdout"]
CHECK_FAIL = GLOBALS["CheckFail"]
MODES = ("ABSENT", "REPLAY", "SNAPSHOT", "MANIFEST", "RECORDER",
         "R033LIVE", "BIB", "LOGBIB", "PDFINFO", "PDFTEXT", "PDFRAW",
         "SOURCEFINAL", "CROSS", "STAGEINV", "EVIDENCE")
if tuple(FIELDS) != MODES or sum(len(value) for value in FIELDS.values()) != 90:
    raise SystemExit("FIELD_CENSUS")
UNIQUE = {name for values in FIELDS.values() for name in values}
SYMBOLIC = {"root", "stage", "checkpoint", "id", "dependencies", "disposition"}
SHA_NAMES = {name for name in UNIQUE if "sha256" in name}
if (len(UNIQUE) != 52 or len(DECIMALS) != 29 or len(SYMBOLIC) != 6 or
        len(SHA_NAMES) != 16 or
        UNIQUE != set(DECIMALS) | SYMBOLIC | {"warning_bytes_hex"} | SHA_NAMES):
    raise SystemExit("FIELD_PARTITION")
H = "0" * 64
O = "1" * 64
R = "R023:" + H + "/" + H + ",R043:" + H + "/" + H + ",R053:" + H + "/" + H
M = ("R009:" + H + "/" + H + ",R024:" + H + "/" + H +
     ",R033:" + H + "/" + H + ",R044:" + H + "/" + H +
     ",R054:" + H + "/" + H)
ID_DEFAULT = {"SNAPSHOT": "R021", "MANIFEST": "R009", "RECORDER": "R023"}
SPECIAL_DECIMAL = {"absent": "1", "stage_empty": "1", "source_files": "3",
                   "raw_pairs": "8", "recorder_pairs": "3",
                   "manifest_pairs": "5", "pre_X010": "1"}

def frame(mode, overrides=None):
    values = {}
    for name in FIELDS[mode]:
        if name in DECIMALS:
            values[name] = SPECIAL_DECIMAL.get(name, "0")
        elif name == "root" or name == "stage":
            values[name] = "r0"
        elif name == "checkpoint":
            values[name] = "R020-pre"
        elif name == "id":
            values[name] = ID_DEFAULT[mode]
        elif name == "dependencies":
            values[name] = "87/86"
        elif name == "disposition":
            values[name] = "benign-underfull-only"
        elif name == "warning_bytes_hex":
            values[name] = "-"
        elif name == "recorder_sha256":
            values[name] = R
        elif name == "manifest_sha256" and mode == "CROSS":
            values[name] = M
        elif "sha256" in name:
            values[name] = H
        else:
            raise SystemExit("UNCLASSIFIED_" + name)
    if overrides:
        values.update(overrides)
    line = "PASS " + mode + " " + " ".join(name + "=" + values[name] for name in FIELDS[mode]) + "\n"
    return line.encode("ascii"), values

def accept(mode, overrides=None, expected=()):
    raw, values = frame(mode, overrides)
    if PARSE(raw, mode, expected, "T") != values:
        raise SystemExit("POSITIVE_" + mode)
    return 1

def reject_raw(raw, mode, suffix, expected=()):
    try:
        PARSE(raw, mode, expected, "T")
    except CHECK_FAIL as error:
        if error.args != ("T" + suffix,):
            raise SystemExit("TAG_" + suffix + "_" + repr(error.args))
    else:
        raise SystemExit("ACCEPTED_" + suffix)
    return 1

def reject(mode, overrides, suffix):
    raw, unused = frame(mode, overrides)
    return reject_raw(raw, mode, suffix)

def render(tokens):
    return (" ".join(tokens) + "\n").encode("ascii")

positive_count = 0
negative_count = 0
for mode in MODES:
    positive_count += accept(mode)
for mode in MODES:
    if "root" in FIELDS[mode]:
        positive_count += accept(mode, {"root": "r1"})
positive_count += accept("STAGEINV", {"stage": "r1"})
for checkpoint in ("R020-pre", "R020-post", "R030-pre", "R030-post",
                   "R040-pre", "R040-post", "R050-pre", "R050-post"):
    positive_count += accept("REPLAY", {"checkpoint": checkpoint})
for identity in ("R009", "R021", "R022", "R023", "R024", "R031", "R032", "R033",
                 "R041", "R042", "R043", "R044", "R051", "R052", "R053", "R054"):
    positive_count += accept("SNAPSHOT", {"id": identity})
positive_count += accept("ABSENT", expected=(("root", "r0"),))

negative_count += reject("ABSENT", {"root": "r2"}, "_ROOT")
negative_count += reject("STAGEINV", {"stage": "r2"}, "_STAGE")
negative_count += reject("REPLAY", {"checkpoint": "R020"}, "_CHECKPOINT")
negative_count += reject("SNAPSHOT", {"id": "R020"}, "_ID")
negative_count += reject("ABSENT", {"dependencies": "86/86"}, "_DEPENDENCIES")
negative_count += reject("LOGBIB", {"disposition": "benign"}, "_DISPOSITION")
for name in sorted(DECIMALS):
    mode = next(candidate for candidate in MODES if name in FIELDS[candidate])
    negative_count += reject(mode, {name: "00"}, "_DECIMAL_" + name)
GENERIC_SHA = sorted(SHA_NAMES - {"recorder_sha256", "manifest_sha256"})
for name in GENERIC_SHA:
    mode = next(candidate for candidate in MODES if name in FIELDS[candidate])
    negative_count += reject(mode, {name: "A" * 64}, "_HASH_" + name)
negative_count += reject("SOURCEFINAL", {"manifest_sha256": "A" * 64}, "_HASH_manifest_sha256")
negative_count += reject("LOGBIB", {"warning_bytes_hex": "a"}, "_WARNING_HEX")
BAD_R = "R023:" + H + "/" + H + ",R043:" + H + "/" + H + ",R053:" + H + "/" + O
BAD_M = ("R009:" + H + "/" + H + ",R024:" + H + "/" + H +
         ",R033:" + H + "/" + H + ",R044:" + H + "/" + H +
         ",R054:" + H + "/" + O)
negative_count += reject("CROSS", {"recorder_sha256": BAD_R}, "_RECORDER_HASHES")
negative_count += reject("CROSS", {"manifest_sha256": BAD_M}, "_MANIFEST_HASHES")

for mode in MODES:
    raw, unused = frame(mode)
    tokens = raw[:-1].decode("ascii").split(" ")
    negative_count += reject_raw(render(tokens[:-1]), mode, "_PREFIX")
    negative_count += reject_raw(render(tokens + ["extra=1"]), mode, "_PREFIX")
    changed = list(tokens)
    changed[2], changed[3] = changed[3], changed[2]
    negative_count += reject_raw(render(changed), mode, "_FIELD_" + FIELDS[mode][0])
    changed = list(tokens)
    changed[3] = changed[2]
    negative_count += reject_raw(render(changed), mode, "_FIELD_" + FIELDS[mode][1])
    changed = list(tokens)
    changed[2] = FIELDS[mode][0] + "="
    negative_count += reject_raw(render(changed), mode, "_FIELD_" + FIELDS[mode][0])

sample, unused = frame("ABSENT")
negative_count += reject_raw(sample[:-1], "ABSENT", "_FRAMING")
negative_count += reject_raw(sample + b"\n", "ABSENT", "_FRAMING")
negative_count += reject_raw(sample[:-1] + b"\r\n", "ABSENT", "_FRAMING")
negative_count += reject_raw(sample[:1] + b"\x00" + sample[1:], "ABSENT", "_FRAMING")
negative_count += reject_raw(sample[:1] + bytes([255]) + sample[1:], "ABSENT", "_FRAMING")
negative_count += reject_raw(sample[:1] + b"\t" + sample[1:], "ABSENT", "_FRAMING")
tokens = sample[:-1].decode("ascii").split(" ")
changed = list(tokens)
changed[0] = "POSS"
negative_count += reject_raw(render(changed), "ABSENT", "_PREFIX")
changed = list(tokens)
changed[1] = "REPLAY"
negative_count += reject_raw(render(changed), "ABSENT", "_PREFIX")
negative_count += reject_raw(b"\n", "UNKNOWN", "_MODE")
negative_count += reject_raw(sample, "ABSENT", "_EXPECTED_root", expected=(("root", "r1"),))

if positive_count != 53 or negative_count != 138:
    raise SystemExit("COUNT_" + str(positive_count) + "_" + str(negative_count))
print("PASS parser_microtest source_sha256=" + SOURCE_SHA256 +
      " modes=15 fields=90 positives=53 negatives=138")
BATCH07_P27_RECOVERY_PARSER_MICROTEST_HARNESS_END

design_disposition: E0314's one-Python-fork plus ctypes/prctl clause is superseded before any successor file or process exists; no silent architecture substitution is allowed
design_finding_1: Python code between fork and exec adds interpreter/allocator/loader state to the child trust boundary and makes child-side error and parent-death handling unnecessarily fragile
design_finding_2: parent-death SIGKILL alone cannot preserve an in-memory report when the direct supervisor dies; a surviving direct payload parent must both kill/reap the payload and perform the read-only binder
design_finding_3: a lost watchdog/report requires an externally known session/process group plus a recovery-binder-only mode after the group is proven gone; generic merged or truncating command capture cannot confer success
corrected_authorized_resolution: create exactly the still-reserved append-only E001_SUPERVISOR_BINDER_RECOVERY.md containing one literal three-mode Python program; exact modes are supervisor, watchdog and recovery-binder; the same frozen binder audit core serves watchdog failure and recovery-binder mode
corrected_no_fork_rule: the literal program may not call fork, subprocess, preexec_fn, ctypes, prctl, eval, compile or dynamic import; both child launches use os.posix_spawn with frozen file actions and empty exec environments
supervisor_mode: require exact cwd/env/flags/argv and a two-pass 0/1/2-only inherited-FD census; create only one CLOEXEC lifeline/start pipe and one CLOEXEC ready pipe; posix_spawn watchdog into a new session with fixed fd10=start-read and fd11=ready-write; close every opposite/original end; reap the exact watchdog
watchdog_handshake: validate exact mode/runtime and fd set 0/1/2/10/11; write exact one-byte R then close fd11; supervisor accepts only R then writes exact one-byte S; watchdog accepts only S; receipt of S is the unique attempt-consumption point; supervisor retains the lifeline writer until watchdog completion
supervisor_loss_rule: EOF on watchdog fd10 before complete reporting sets supervisor_lost=1, makes success impossible, sends one SIGKILL to any live payload, drains both payload pipes, reaps it and runs the in-process read-only binder; watchdog writes its canonical report directly to the external stdout pipe rather than through supervisor
payload_spawn: only after exact S, watchdog creates one CLOEXEC payload-stdout pipe and one CLOEXEC payload-stderr pipe; posix_spawn exactly /usr/bin/env with the frozen nine-element E0280 argv and empty environment, mapping only live fd0 plus the two pipe writers to fd1/fd2 and closing fd10 plus every original pipe fd in the payload
payload_capture: watchdog concurrently polls raw payload stdout, raw payload stderr and supervisor lifeline; independent EOF, exact byte caps, monotonic deadline, one SIGKILL on timeout/overflow/lifeline loss, drain and exact waitpid exit/signal/core classification are mandatory; no PTY, merged stream, temp, tee or shell substitution
watchdog_binder: on every failed payload conjunction, call the literal read-only binder core in-process before reporting; never spawn a second payload or mutate evidence
recovery_binder_mode: permitted only when the attempt was consumed and no complete valid watchdog report exists or external capture/status is inconsistent; the external actor first SIGKILLs the known watchdog session PGID, proves the group absent, preserves the single-writer interval, then invokes the same literal program once in recovery-binder mode; this mode cannot reach payload spawn code
corrected_phase_schema: retain E0314's conservative last-present-child-durability-unproven phases; recovery-binder with lost transcript/status reports durability_phase=unknown-mismatch and disposition=PERMANENT_FAILURE; no four-file physical state can imply success
corrected_candidate_schema: every known literal's record includes absent-ENOENT or exact type/dev/ino/full-mode/nlink/uid/gid/rdev/bytes/LF/SHA plus all candidate duplicate and source-equal dev/ino pairs; unknown inventory names are raw-hex only and never opened
canonical_reporting: watchdog alone emits one bounded canonical ASCII/LF result; success is a frozen exact literal distinct from raw payload PASS; failure has fixed field order, canonical decimals/enums/lowercase hashes/even hex and exact caps; close internal descriptors before direct write-all and _exit; watchdog exit0 means complete report, not payload success
external_trust_boundary: later activation must bind an exact non-PTY separate-binary-pipe actor that knows the supervisor/watchdog session PGID, concurrently drains through EOF without truncation, reaps the direct supervisor, rejects every stderr byte and any malformed/incomplete report, invokes recovery-binder after PGID kill on report loss, and appends the physical ledger result while the single-writer interval remains held
external_actor_loss_rule: durable executor metadata must retain the consumed-attempt bit and known watchdog session PGID before S can be delivered; without that named durable recovery fact, later execution review must fail
microtest_requirement: after successor author stop and dual static PASS, isolated no-build microtests must cover handshake, dual-stream deadlock/LF, exit/signal/timeout/overflow, supervisor loss, watchdog/report loss, PGID kill, report truncation and recovery-binder dispatch; microtests never use the real payload or a build path
old_failure_preservation: E0314 and its rejected fork/prctl clause remain immutable historical reasoning; E001_FIRST_COPY_RECOVERY.md and W2 failure remain unchanged; no E001/build access occurred
successor_review_threshold: X1/X2 plus later isolated microtest-plan reviewers must be separated and all-zero; any finding stops without control activation or payload execution

V4_capture_transition_resolution: no direct wait-present-and-streams-empty break exists; COMPLETE requires a timely payload wait, both timely EOFs and zero deadline bits, while unsafe kill/reap or EOF-grace expiry exits nonzero without an authoritative direct result
V4_kill_reap_resolution: after kill, waitpid continues under a new absolute kill/reap deadline even when the payload deadline already fired; post-wait time is checked before status commit, and supervisor cleanup uses the same post-observation ordering
V4_terminal_evidence_resolution: initial evidence final-path observation occurs only after snapshots one and two, terminal evidence final-path observation occurs only after snapshot three, and both retained records bind the pathname after all observations they bracket before phase classification
V4_recovery_schema_resolution: allocate and retain the full recovery audit before any input construction; guard FailureBinderInputs, evidence-parent Chain, binder, verification, close and render paths independently; record the second ESRCH proof before attempting Chain; ordinary unavailable input/evidence failures render the complete permanent-failure schema only while all required group-absence proofs remain valid

wait_commit_rule: exact waitpid return shall be committed immediately into the same preallocated stable slot without allocation or user callback; any later status-validation or reporting error demotes but cannot resurrect, lose or abandon that physically reaped ownership record
registry_failure_rule: every pre-spawn reservation, post-return commit and cleanup transition shall use the fixed registry; cleanup shall conservatively visit every reserved/live/unknown slot and no dynamic map, sort or role list may be its only census; a reserved slot may be released without signaling only when spawn noncreation is positively established
cleanup_error_containment_rule: cleanup is a non-throwing exhaustive state machine over the fixed census; every per-slot signal, wait, deadline, state or close error is latched and accumulated without aborting later slots, and a premise-bounded rescue continues until every created PID is exact-reaped; only after registry emptiness may reporting occur, and no cleanup exception may escape finally with a live or unknown slot
cleanup_order_correction: broker admission closes first; child slots are exact-PID stopped and reaped before marker, marker before launcher, and launcher before keeper; hold writers or other liveness gates for launcher and keeper remain open until their own ordered stop transition and cannot use premature EOF as an unordered substitute; keeper is the last exact-PID stop and reap
probe_broker_mapping_rule: Host V9 shall bind each of all fifteen probe IDs to exactly either one of the seven broker operations or a local-no-broker branch; outer enforces that exact mapping, reads no mandatory request for a local branch, accepts exactly one authenticated request for a broker branch, and after marker reap proves EOF with zero late, duplicate, partial or surplus request bytes before PASS
child_result_validation_rule: every broker operation validates the exact expected physical raw status, output length and bytes, mode/source/image/environment observation and operation-specific semantics before response; P09 proves SIGKILL status, P10 proves sixteen successful INFO observations and distinct physical PIDs, and launcher plus keeper require their exact expected termination status; reap alone is never semantic success
result_framing_rule: all result fields are preinitialized before any fallible operation; exact write-all logic with bounded progress and mandatory post-write checks emits the complete marker result and terminal report, and any EOF, EPIPE, short write or framing exception latches failure and cannot exit status zero or claim authoritative PASS
deadline_rule: every fallible or blocking call, EOF return, successful poll, exact wait return, output drain, signal transition and branch completion receives a mandatory immediate post-call deadline check before break, return, response or PASS; cleanup uses its separately derived premise-backed bound and no fresh cleanup clock may erase an already-detected operational overrun
fd_ownership_hardening_rule: every pipe or other local descriptor is either entered into a fixed ownership table immediately on creation or closed by a non-throwing local finally on every spawn-success, spawn-failure, E2BIG, validation, deadline and cleanup edge; descriptor leakage cannot be hidden by outer process exit
derived_cleanup_bound_rule_V9: derive an overflow-checked finite guard from MAX_LIVE_SLOTS, OWNER_CONTROL_PROGRESS_NS, TERM allowance, corrected KILL_REAP_PROGRESS_NS, finite syscall/EINTR overhead, ordered gate closure and keeper finalization; list each arithmetic term and prove the same bound covers enumeration, admission close, pre-signal progress, exact kill/reap, error rescue and final framing under the explicit premises
observation_premise_rule: no successful observation, ACK, EOF, elapsed grace, signal syscall return, process exit, ESRCH, ancestor reap or one passing run may be used to prove the corrected premises; they are explicit actor/environment preconditions that require a later separately reviewed actor successor before execution

terminal_framing_progress_term: bind a positive finite TERMINAL_FRAMING_PROGRESS_NS or an exact overflow-checked maximum count of terminal framing transitions multiplied by OWNER_CONTROL_PROGRESS_NS; it covers receiver drain, each short-write continuation, EINTR retry, post-write check and exit-status decision; EPIPE, receiver close or premise violation cannot claim PASS and must yield nonzero or no-authoritative-result rather than an incomplete status-zero success

finding_U01_id: active-actor-calls-undefined-runtime-registration-helper
finding_U01_fact: active actor source calls register_runtime_fd at three reachable sites, including verify_external_inputs on the main entry path, but actor raw source has no definition or assignment for that name; only the watchdog span defines it, so the actor cannot reach READY or BEGIN
runner_V15_U01_resolution: define and use an actor-local bounded runtime-observation ownership helper before every actor call; its registry, identity capture, proved-close reconciliation, exception contract and call arities must be self-contained in the actor span, or remove every call only by replacing it with an equally exhaustive actor-local primitive; no cross-source name assumption is permitted
finding_U02_id: acquisition-SCM-rights-and-endpoint-adoption-precede-exhaustive-ownership
finding_U02_fact_1: watchdog cap_status, proc_starttime and mount_binding open observation descriptors without registry ownership and close them through raw close_numbers; a same-identity close failure unwinds and loses the only number while the exhaustive predicate later sees only registered slots
finding_U02_fact_2: register_lifecycle_fd performs fallible checks, lookup, tuple/journal construction and dictionary installation before a provisional owning slot is guaranteed; an opened root or kill descriptor can survive a failed install outside cleanup-by-slot
finding_U02_fact_3: SCM_RIGHTS intake performs fallible ancillary decoding and allocation before every installed descriptor is quarantined or registered; a failure can leave an installed right outside the persistent registry and later release predicate
finding_U02_fact_4: control and external endpoint validation directly close socket objects, while static_inputs acquires both in one return expression and adopts them into lifecycle registry only after return; failure can produce an untracked close or temporarily owned socket outside registry
finding_U02_minimal_trace: root kill open succeeds; provisional installation fails; containment cleanup names only registry slots and no-ops; later all registered entries close and owner_released becomes true while the unregistered writable fd survives
runner_V15_U02_resolution_1: preallocate a fixed typed lifecycle record for every possible actor/watchdog acquisition role before any fd-producing operation; acquisition marks the reserved record ACQUIRING, stores the returned raw number in that same record immediately before any validation, identity, journal or other fallible work, and on any pre-adoption exception strict-close/reconciles the exact raw local number before unwinding
runner_V15_U02_resolution_2: route cap_status, proc_starttime, mount_binding and every observational helper through that primitive; their proved-close state must remain in the exhaustive registry until closure is known, and helper unwinding may never discard a live number
runner_V15_U02_resolution_3: receive SCM_RIGHTS into bounded preallocated quarantine roles; before semantic decoding or validation, each kernel-installed fd is either installed into its reserved quarantine record or strict-close/reconciled from an explicit raw-local fallback; any ancillary failure walks and resolves every installed right, and no right can exist solely in a transient decoded container
runner_V15_U02_resolution_4: acquire, register and validate control and external endpoints sequentially rather than in one return expression; validation failure closes through the lifecycle primitive, socket wrappers cannot directly close adopted fds, and every endpoint is registry-owned before the next acquisition
finding_U03_id: promotion-and-proved-close-journal-transitions-are-not-atomic
finding_U03_fact_1: promote_lifecycle_fd deactivates and clears the source slot before fallible destination installation; failure leaves a live descriptor with no owning registry entry
finding_U03_fact_2: after physical close or EBADF reconciliation, lifecycle_mark_closed performs fallible journal/update work before authoritative slot transition; a later fd reuse can make retry close the wrong object because stored identity is not revalidated first
finding_U03_fact_3: recovery manually clears stage_fd after closing a different recovery-stage slot, violating same-slot proved-close ownership
runner_V15_U03_resolution_1: promotion is an in-place role transition on one preallocated lifecycle record or an atomic alias swap in which the source remains the owner until the destination is irrevocably live; no fallible allocation, journal append or dictionary insertion may occur inside the ownership handoff
runner_V15_U03_resolution_2: proved-close state mutation is nonallocating and authoritative before any optional audit-journal append; every retry first revalidates the stored dev/inode/type identity, global live-fd-number uniqueness is enforced, and a reused or mismatched number becomes retained fault rather than a close target
runner_V15_U03_resolution_3: prohibit all manual ownership-slot minus-one or provenance clears; only the same slot's proved-close transition can clear its number, while cached causal provenance remains separately immutable
finding_U04_id: fixed-enumeration-omits-live-dynamic-capabilities-and-unique-kill-proof
finding_U04_fact_1: external_capabilities enumerates only a fixed slot table plus two special slots and never compares against ownership_transfer_keys; live dynamic stage, containment, stream or outer receive slots can be omitted from the 46-pair offer
finding_U04_fact_2: actor still opens and sends a same-leaf writable cgroup.kill right while ROOT_KILL_FD is retained; if stream_kill_received proved-close fails, unique_kill_authority sees it but offer construction does not call that invariant and can transfer ROOT_KILL_FD while duplicate writable authority remains local
runner_V15_U04_resolution_1: derive the transferable offer set from the exhaustive registry, selecting every live transferable record exactly once in canonical role order; compare the constructed capability-key set byte-for-byte with the registry-derived expected set before reservation, immediately before send and at acceptance, rejecting any missing, extra, alias or duplicate authority
runner_V15_U04_resolution_2: remove actor KILL_FD from the active protocol entirely: actor opens and sends no writable kill descriptor, ARM schemas and rights counts contain no KILL_FD, watchdog uses already bound ROOT_KILL_FD as the sole local and transferable kill capability, and containment/leaf validation uses non-writable identity evidence
runner_V15_U04_resolution_3: unique_kill_authority is a mandatory invariant before kill call, offer freeze, send activation and acceptance commit; receiver acceptance proves exactly one writable kill capability in the complete exhaustive set, not merely absence of a literal KILL_FD kind from an incomplete tuple
finding_U05_id: accepted-and-direct-partial-closure-cannot-resume
finding_U05_fact_1: close_ownership_capabilities closes nonendpoints including root rights and pidfds, then crosses fallible checkpoints before endpoint close; generic BaseException changes durable COMMITTED acceptance to TRANSFER_CLOSURE_CAP_HOLD and every retry refuses to reenter committed closure
finding_U05_fact_2: direct terminal partial close has no same-cursor retry; fallback attempts a new generic offer after required root rights and fd4/fd15 may already be closed, while pollers and external transport still use hard-coded closed pidfds and can treat POLLNVAL as readiness
finding_U05_minimal_generic_trace: durable acceptance commits; nonendpoints close; checkpoint fails; state downgrades from COMMITTED; retry is rejected forever while endpoints remain held and no resend is permitted
runner_V15_U05_resolution_1: durable acceptance state COMMITTED is immutable; ownership_close_started and a separate monotone closure cursor record the direct or accepted close phase, and every exception or fallback resumes the same cursor without offer rebuild, resend, sequence mutation or state downgrade
runner_V15_U05_resolution_2: perform every nonownership progression checkpoint before the first irreversible ownership close; after closure starts, only per-slot close/reconciliation work and the exhaustive predicate gate progress, with no deadline/checkpoint exception capable of abandoning the cursor
runner_V15_U05_resolution_3: direct terminal closure uses the identical cursor and retry entry; once started it can never route to generic offer construction; closed pidfds are removed from poll sets, POLLNVAL is an error not readiness, and all later logic consumes cached causal facts rather than hard-coded fd4/fd15
runner_V15_U05_resolution_4: endpoint close is journaled as the final ownership phase; an already-closed endpoint is never required for retry or acknowledgement, and exhaustive local closure permits logical release even if later nonownership reporting fails
finding_M01_id: pre-action-endpoint-adoption-direct-close-and-tuple-acquisition
finding_M01_fact: acquire_control and acquire_external_owner directly close registry-owned descriptors on validation failure, and static_inputs binds both returned socket objects only after a combined expression completes; this pre-BEGIN path violates the same exhaustive adoption contract even where it cannot yet reach post-BEGIN release
runner_V15_M01_resolution: include all pre-action endpoints in U02's sequential preallocated acquisition/adoption primitive, forbid direct socket.close on adopted numbers, and statically prove no temporary socket object owns an fd outside the registry across a second acquisition
runner_V14_disposition: immutable failed supervisor-prebind history with no manifest row; exact bytes, identities and both complete FAIL reports remain preserved; no edit-in-place, formal review, execution, reinterpretation or retroactive PASS
